local.name: Elliptic K via AGM
local.description: Complete elliptic integral of the first kind using the arithmetic-geometric mean.

classifications.notes: The README defines K(k) with modulus k, lists supporting-module dependencies and describes precision variants. Optional real128 support depends on the compiler; parameter/modulus conventions must be respected in future drivers.

The inspected REAL64 elliptic_k overload evaluates the complete Legendre elliptic integral of the first kind with modulus k. It forms the complementary modulus as sqrt((1-k)*(1+k)); for k*k<0.5 it returns (pi/2)/AGM(1,k-prime), and otherwise uses an AGM/elliptic-nome logarithmic transformation. C14 is the elliptic-integrals leaf in this taxonomy; complete first-kind scope is recorded in the procedure rather than inventing a narrower code. IEEE branches return quiet NaN for NaN input or |k|>1 and positive infinity for |k|=1. Material limitation: although the interface advertises |k|<=1, the second branch calls arithmetic_geometric_mean_kernel(1,k), not AGM(1,abs(k)); negative k with k*k>=0.5 therefore reaches a signed-input dependency path and must not be assumed valid. The sketch uses nonnegative modulus and the simple direct branch. Dependencies are unpinned Git references in fpm.toml, and their full AGM/nome algorithms are outside this review. The committed module unconditionally imports/declares REAL128 as well as REAL32/64, so its build needs that kind despite README calling it optional. No integral or reference test was executed.

local.name: KFAS
local.description: R state-space modeling software with Fortran kernels for Kalman filtering and smoothing.

classifications.notes: The README and DESCRIPTION document Gaussian/non-Gaussian state-space inference, filtering and smoothing. This is an R package with compiled numerical components, not a ready-made standalone Fortran API.

KFILTER performs sequential-observation Kalman filtering for a linear Gaussian state-space model, including optional exact diffuse initialization via P1INF/RANKP. The inspected ordinary branch updates innovations, gain, mean/covariance and log likelihood, then propagates the state with T and R*Q*R^T. TIMEVAR has five 0/1 selectors controlling third-dimension lengths of Z,H,T,R,Q. YMISS=0 means observed; positive missing flags skip measurement updates. The scalar-observation sketch avoids the requirement to transform correlated multivariate measurement errors before sequential filtering: the core uses diagonal H entries. AT(:,t) and PT(:,:,t) are prediction states before observation t; the optional THETA output uses those predictions and is not a smoothed estimate. Likelihood accumulation and tolerance-based zero-innovation handling do not certify covariance positivity or model fit. Review covers driver and ordinary/diffuse one-step recurrences, not every R-facing data transformation or non-Gaussian smoother.

local.name: KernelyzeBase
local.description: Low-rank approximation of bivariate kernel functions.

classifications.notes: The README describes separable rank-reduced representations and sign-regular kernels. Optimality and comparative error claims are author statements; the entry is classified as approximation rather than a generic interpolation solver.

EIGEN_RANKN_PARAMS forms sqrt(Wx)*K*sqrt(Wy), computes a dense SVD and constructs Nystrom coefficients for separated singular-function kernel approximation, with X_FUNC_WTS sized (NY,RANK) and Y_FUNC_WTS (NX,RANK). This is a quadrature-discretized approximation for a supplied concrete two-variable kernel; it is not a uniform/global minimax error certificate. Although input guards allow nonnegative weights, later code divides by their square roots, so supply strictly positive finite weights; retained singular values must be nonzero before reciprocal scaling. Rank must be positive and no larger than either point count. No extra guard handles zero retained singular values, numerical rank deficiency or ill-conditioned kernels. The review covers this selected approximation path, not every numerically-optimal/rank-reduction algorithm in the larger library.

local.name: polynomial_interpolation
local.description: Lagrange interpolation with derivative estimates and an interpolation-quality indicator.

classifications.notes: The README documents arbitrary data points and an auxiliary grid-to-grid interpolation routine. An error indicator is not described as a rigorously certified error bound.

poly_interp implements a Neville-style Lagrange correction recurrence for the polynomial through n+1 distinct samples, also propagating derivative corrections. It evaluates at zero, so callers shift their abscissae by the desired query. This is a single polynomial (E1b), distinct from the local moving-stencil grid wrapper. Output y(0) is the value and y(k) is derivative k, not divided Taylor coefficients. dy is the last signed interpolation correction, not a certified error bound. There is no input-validation/status interface; duplicate nodes divide by zero. Restrict this reviewed use to n >= 1 and 0 <= nd <= n: for n=0 or derivative orders beyond n, some dy entries need not be assigned. Accuracy, conditioning and behavior on closely spaced nodes were not checked by execution.

local.name: spharm-interp
local.description: Scattered-data fitting and interpolation on the sphere using spherical harmonic expansions.

classifications.notes: The README describes least-squares fitting followed by expansion evaluation. Drivers use MATLAB/Octave with Fortran MEX kernels; author demonstration errors are not catalog-verified results.

The selected ylgndr recurrence evaluates normalized associated Legendre functions for nonnegative degree/order, n<=nmax and 0<=m<=n, at finite x in [-1,1]. The normalization is sqrt(2*n+1)*sqrt((n-m)!/(n+m)!)*P_nm(x), with the negative diagonal square-root recurrence incorporating the Condon-Shortley sign. Only the lower triangle of y is assigned; other entries are undefined. There is no domain/status check or derivative output in this selected routine. This Fortran special-function mapping is separate from the MATLAB scattered-point fit and does not establish high-degree stability by execution.

local.name: SPRINT
local.description: Grid interpolation with bilinear interpolator interfaces and cached point weights.

classifications.notes: The inspected source interface identifies regular and curvilinear grids and cached weights. Periodic boundary handling is explicitly a TODO; source-interface inspection is not a full implementation or numerical review.

The inspected structured-grid path prepares four tensor-product bilinear weights from normalized x/y coordinates, caches them by a formatted coordinate key, and applies them to four supplied values. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation; the type does not fetch a full field or perform three-/four-coordinate interpolation (higher-rank values carry extra fields). Important source defects prevent a general-use recommendation: REAL(8) regular-grid preparation uses FLOOR without the required one-based offset and leaves the fourth corner second index zero by writing corner 3 twice; REAL(4) uses CEILING but excludes the lower endpoint and accepts some cells past the final valid interval. apply calls prepare on a cache miss but computes its result only in the ELSE branch, leaving the first return undefined unless prepare is called explicitly. apply neither guards outside points nor checks value-array extents. Its corner order is (lower-left, lower-right, upper-right, upper-left) mapped to input positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2), not the usual rectangular-field order. The sketch is a restricted REAL(4), strictly interior, explicitly prepared interface illustration. Curvilinear location/inversion and dependencies are not audited. No interpolation or defect was reproduced by execution.

use bilinear_interpolator_mod, only: bilinear_interpolator_type
type(bilinear_interpolator_type) :: interp

corners(2,1)=1.0

The selected fixed-form TRIPACK TRMESH routine incrementally constructs an unconstrained planar Delaunay triangulation in linked adjacency storage. It initializes a noncollinear triangle, inserts nodes and swaps edges using orientation/circumcircle tests and nearest-node search starts. Require distinct coordinates and a noncollinear first triple. LIST/LPTR need 6*N-12 storage, LEND/NEAR/NEXT/DIST need N. IER distinguishes invalid size, initial collinearity, duplicate nodes and internal swap failure; partial adjacency is not a completed mesh on failure. This is planar triangulation rather than spherical geometry or a PDE discretization. The selected fixed-form source uses default REAL and is included by SRFPACK; the separate tripack.f90 variant uses REAL(8) and must not be mixed blindly with these call declarations. Review covers construction and storage contracts, not robust exact predicates or every constrained-edge operation.

DMRGG_LIB::DTT_DMRGG adaptively samples a tensor-valued function at selected multi-indices, updates TT cross pivots/cores and increases bond ranks. It uses MPI distribution/communication and optional OpenMP callback evaluation; the callback has the positional convention FUN(M,IND,N,PAR). MAXRANK bounds growth and ACCURACY tests sampled pivot magnitude relative to a reference for three consecutive strikes, not a rigorous global residual bound over every tensor entry. The routine wipes an incoming nonempty TT state to rank-one initialization. Require initialized MPI with number of ranks strictly less than tensor dimension M, positive mode sizes, valid callback parameters, consistent precision and safe indices. Some diagnostics read ME before MPI_COMM_RANK initialization. This review covers the adaptive driver and inspected pivot/termination paths, not all lower-level max-volume/inversion kernels, every process partition or the optional quadrature application.

double precision :: parameters(1)

approximation%m=3; approximation%n(1:3)=[2,2,2]
parameters=1.0d0

     accuracy=1.0d-6,maxrank=4)
call dealloc(approximation)

classifications.notes: The README documents HFTI, NNLS, BVLS and related routines and modern interfaces. Additional SVD/rotation utilities are noted but not all mapped to separate classes in this review.

The legacy NNLS routine initializes x=0, selects columns using the largest positive dual-gradient component, applies Householder transformations, solves the passive triangular system, and uses a feasibility interpolation/Givens update loop to move nonpositive coefficients back to the zero set. classifications.notes: The reviewed README lists trapezoidal, Simpson and Gaussian methods. The repository formerly listed as IntegralALL now resolves to PyIntegral; the catalog uses the current canonical repository identity.

The external GAUSSLEGENDREQUADRATURE routine generates successive n-point Gauss-Legendre rules with polynomial recurrence/Newton root refinement, linearly interpolates tabulated X/Y at those nodes and returns the last weighted sum. This is nonautomatic finite-interval quadrature of gridded data, not a callback integrator or accuracy-controlled algorithm. N_INT is the last quadrature order, not a tolerance. local.name: GALAHAD
local.description: Modern Fortran optimization packages for constrained/unconstrained, linear/quadratic and least-squares problems.

classifications.notes: The README documents a broad collection and several language interfaces. Individual algorithms, optional linear solvers and problem subclasses need their own procedure reviews; availability of a release binary is not catalog verification.

EQP solves equality-constrained quadratic subproblems through projected/preconditioned iterative work with dependency removal and sparse block factorizations. The concrete sketch has positive-definite H=2I, so its mapping is the convex quadratic-program class G2e1; this does not assert that all library EQP problems require positive-definite H on the full space. Public QPT data stores the constraint constant C in A*x+C=0, as the native example and feasibility RHS=-C show, despite the solve prologue shorthand A*x=c. H uses its lower triangle in coordinate storage. The sketch sets Hessian_kind=-1 to select the supplied Hessian explicitly. The source module name is precision-preprocessed; GALAHAD_EQP_double is the author-example public double-precision facade. Match its integer ABI and configured sparse/dense factorization backends. INITIALIZE/SOLVE/TERMINATE form the lifecycle; TERMINATE overwrites INFORM, so retain solve diagnostics first. Review covers the public solver, author data layout and selected native dispatch/stopping paths, not every linear algebra backend or a numerical verification.

procedures.summary: Public double-precision convex equality-constrained quadratic-program driver.
procedures.usage:
program quadratic_sketch
use GALAHAD_EQP_double
implicit none
integer,parameter :: wp=kind(1d0)
integer :: status
type(QPT_problem_type) :: p
type(EQP_data_type) :: data
type(EQP_control_type) :: control
type(EQP_inform_type) :: inform
p%n=2; p%m=1; p%f=0._wp; p%new_problem_structure=.true.
allocate(p%G(2),p%C(1),p%X(2),p%Y(1))
p%X=0._wp; p%Y=0._wp
p%Hessian_kind=-1; p%G=[-2._wp,-4._wp]; p%C=[-1._wp]
! EQP interprets the equality as A*X + C = 0.
call SMT_put(p%H%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "H storage allocation failed"
call SMT_put(p%A%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "A storage allocation failed"
allocate(p%H%val(2),p%H%row(2),p%H%col(2))
allocate(p%A%val(2),p%A%row(2),p%A%col(2))
p%H%ne=2; p%H%row=[1,2]; p%H%col=[1,2]
p%H%val=[2._wp,2._wp]
p%A%ne=2; p%A%row=[1,1]; p%A%col=[1,2]; p%A%val=1._wp
call EQP_initialize(data,control,inform)
control%SBLS_control%symmetric_linear_solver="sytr"
control%FDC_control%symmetric_linear_solver="sytr"
call EQP_solve(p,data,control,inform)
if(inform%status/=0) then
 print *,"solver status",inform%status
else
 print *,inform%obj,p%X
end if
! Preserve solve status before termination, which overwrites INFORM.
call EQP_terminate(data,control,inform)
end program

local.name: GADfit
local.description: Joint nonlinear curve fitting with shared parameters and automatic differentiation.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly uses global fitting to mean fitting multiple datasets with shared parameters. It does not establish guaranteed global-minimum optimization; modified Levenberg-Marquardt is the documented fitting method.

GADF_FIT performs modified Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares on model functions defined with ADVAR arithmetic. It forms weighted residuals/Jacobians, sums normal-equation contributions across images, solves a damped system and optionally applies a directional second-derivative/geodesic correction. With USE_AD true, the user supplies the model expression rather than analytic derivative routines. Global fitting here means simultaneous datasets with shared parameters, not global optimization. The selected sketch follows the author single-dataset Gaussian setup with error mode NONE; other weighting modes change the objective. Call GADF_INIT, add datasets, mark active parameters and then fit. Data arrays are pointer-associated on input and need valid lifetime/targets. Coarray and preprocessing support plus compatible numerical libraries are required. The code repeatedly combines PRESENT with optional-argument access in logical expressions; strict evaluation/absent-option safety needs separate audit. No complete numerical fit or termination/covariance validation was run.

procedures.summary: Public module damped nonlinear-fit coordinator. Optional scalar tuning arguments such as LAMBDA are REAL32; internal model precision KP is configured separately.

use gadfit

call gadf_add_dataset(x_data,y_data)
! Set parameter values and active flags with GADF_SET first.
call gadf_set_errors(NONE)
call gadf_fit(0.1, max_iter=20, use_ad=.true.)
call gadf_close()

A stopped fit is not proof of a global minimum or calibrated parameter errors.

classifications.notes: The AD module overloads arithmetic on ADVAR, carrying primal VAL, directional derivative D and second directional derivative DD in forward mode, and recording a tape in reverse mode. The selected multiplication path explicitly applies first/second product rules and uses INDEX/=0 to mark active operands. Setting derivative seeds without a nonzero INDEX leaves an operand inactive. The sketch selects forward mode and direct multiplication rather than the integer-power path, whose derivative formula divides by X and Y and needs care at zero even for mathematically regular powers. This is automatic differentiation of the executed operations, not finite differences or symbolic differentiation, and does not make discontinuous branch choices differentiable. Shared module tape/mode state requires coordinated lifetime/thread use; reverse-mode tape capacity and all transcendental branches were not audited.

local.name: Fast Critical Line Algorithm
local.description: Fortran implementation of Markowitz critical-line portfolio optimization.

classifications.notes: The README identifies historical MATLAB/Python bindings and explicitly warns that MEX tricks require adaptation for 64-bit systems. No modern MATLAB or compiler compatibility is implied.

calcturningpoints follows active-set changes along a Markowitz quadratic-program frontier, starting with the largest-mean single component. It updates a restricted covariance inverse when a component enters/leaves, forms affine weights satisfying sum(w)=1 and stores turning-point means, standard deviations, weights and multipliers. G2e1 is scoped to the convex positive-definite covariance case with nonnegative weights and a budget equality, not a generic QP API or the separate arbitrary-bound variant. NN>=2, distinct/nondegenerate means and adequate MAX_TPS are caller assumptions; covariance definiteness and denominator/pivot safety are not checked. Helpers use unpivoted elimination and inverse updates. Some degeneracies leave a zero candidate index, and turning-point output capacity is checked only after the initial stored point. On failure N_TPS can be undefined and early-return allocation cleanup is incomplete. Check ERROR_FLAG before reading valid output prefixes, then verify feasibility/frontier conditions independently. No frontier or QP residual was run.

classifications.notes: The README gives the library scope; Distribution_tools source documentation lists density, distribution, quantile, moment and sampling interfaces. local.name: gfsolver
local.description: Hybrid Newton-bisection root finding for scalar functions.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes switching from basic Newton to a hybrid method after the iteration limit. Bracketing conditions, derivative callbacks and failure handling need further review.

The inspected module solves a scalar real equation through function-value and first-derivative subroutine callbacks; the dummy vectors have length one. sub_newton takes Newton steps and attempts a sign-changing bracket after its Newton iteration limit, then calls sub_hybrid_nb, which bisects when a Newton trial leaves its current interval. F1b describes general nonpolynomial scalar root finding; this is not polynomial root enumeration, a derivative-free interface or a square-system solver. The hybrid code updates the first endpoint when f(x)<0, so its input pair must have the matching sign orientation; it does not validate a bracket on entry. Failure paths print and STOP rather than returning a status, and the Newton path divides by df before testing for a small derivative. The optional fnorm on direct Newton success stores the residual computed before the final x update. The fallback call does not forward the optional tolerance or iteration controls, so the hybrid defaults apply there. Convergence, singular-derivative behavior and all bracket assumptions were not checked by execution.

classifications.notes: The README documents geometric-scale detection and Python-driven examples requiring gfortran. It is a diagnostic workflow, not a general-purpose standalone Fortran interpolation API.

The bundled DELAUNAYSPARSES routine locates Delaunay simplices containing specified query points and returns vertex indices and barycentric weights. Its native serial path constructs a starting simplex, performs a budgeted visibility walk, and optionally projects out-of-hull queries. This source review selects the bundled Fortran geometry, not the Python Delaunay-density diagnostic or an execution check of high-dimensional conditioning.

The vector overload exploits ascending queries using a moving search window and returns endpoint indices outside the grid. N5b records insertion/bracketing-position search, with this interpolation-specific clamping convention rather than a general upper_bound API. Require SIZE(x)>=2, nonempty sorted xp for the vector overload, and finite, distinct ascending grid values. Exact-knot conventions differ: the vector path can return 1 at the first knot, whereas the scalar path starts at 2. The EGM variant intentionally uses a left-of-grid sentinel 1 and differs again at knots; it is not substituted silently. No search result, speed comparison or interpolation was run.

local.name: PDHGEQZ
local.description: Parallel QZ iteration for generalized eigenvalues and generalized Schur forms.

classifications.notes: The driver documentation describes generalized eigenvalues and optional Schur reductions of the input pair. This is a QZ-stage implementation, not an asserted end-to-end solver for every arbitrary matrix-pair representation.

PDHGEQZ computes generalized eigenvalue pairs of a distributed real nonsymmetric Hessenberg/upper-triangular pencil, optionally overwriting it with generalized real Schur form and accumulating left/right orthogonal Schur factors. The native driver dispatches small/large QZ kernels, with shift/deflation work in the distributed implementation. This entry assumes H already upper Hessenberg and T upper triangular; it is not a complete arbitrary dense-pencil reduction in one call. Eigenvalues are represented by (ALPHAR+i*ALPHAI,BETA); retain that representation for zero/tiny BETA instead of blindly dividing. Schur vectors are not individual generalized eigenvectors. MPI/BLACS context, block-cyclic descriptors and local storage must match on all ranks. Query both real and integer workspace after setup; nonzero INFO can mean invalid input or algorithmic failure and no residual/conditioning guarantee follows from zero alone. Review covers public dispatch, workspace contract and selected QZ/deflation paths, not every tuning variant or backend.

procedures.summary: External distributed generalized real QZ driver for a prepared Hessenberg-triangular pencil.

external :: pdhgeqz
integer :: info,ldwork,liwork,integer_query(1)
integer,allocatable :: iwork(:)
double precision :: real_query(1)
double precision,allocatable :: dwork(:)
! After MPI/BLACS setup: H Hessenberg, T triangular, matching descriptors,
! allocated Q/Z storage and replicated ALPHAR/ALPHAI/BETA vectors of length N.
call pdhgeqz("S","I","I",n,1,n,h,desch,t,desct,alphar,alphai,beta, &
 q,descq,z,descz,real_query,-1,integer_query,-1,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "QZ workspace query failed"
ldwork=max(1,ceiling(real_query(1))); liwork=max(1,integer_query(1))
allocate(dwork(ldwork),iwork(liwork))
call pdhgeqz("S","I","I",n,1,n,h,desch,t,desct,alphar,alphai,beta, &
 q,descq,z,descz,dwork,ldwork,iwork,liwork,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect QZ diagnostics"
! Preserve homogeneous eigenvalue pairs when BETA is zero or tiny.

The reviewed CGL path generates Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a,b], produces alternating barycentric weights with half endpoint weights, and evaluates a single univariate global Lagrange polynomial by the barycentric quotient. A near-node isclose test returns the stored sample rather than dividing by a small node difference. E1b records a single polynomial, not a piecewise interpolant or noisy-data fit. n is polynomial degree and arrays need n+1 elements despite some abbreviated shape comments. bary_weights only implements CGL weights, so the sketch does not combine it with CG/CGR nodes. Explicitly pass is_descending=.false.: the node generator default flag has declaration initialization and therefore retains a prior supplied value between calls. Positive n, distinct endpoints and adequate array extents are caller responsibilities; no error estimate/status is returned. Module imports require MKL BLAS95/F95_PRECISION even though this reviewed scalar interpolation path uses no BLAS operation. No interpolation result, extrapolation behavior or alternate node family was verified by execution.

local.name: L-BFGS
local.description: Limited-memory quasi-Newton unconstrained optimization with a CMake build.

classifications.notes: The README identifies Nocedal limited-memory unconstrained optimization and repackaging with a C/C++ header. No bound-constrained capability or global-minimum guarantee is inferred.

The inspected LBFGS path constructs a limited-memory inverse-Hessian action from stored step/gradient-difference pairs, uses a More-Thuente-style MCSRCH line search and requests function/gradient values through reverse communication. The user supplies first derivatives, not a Hessian; G1b1b records smooth multivariate unconstrained minimization. DIAGCO optionally requests a positive diagonal scaling through IFLAG=2. The normal stopping test is ||G||/max(1,||X||)<=EPS after a completed line search; no global-optimality or local-minimum certificate is implied. The initial step is 1/||G|| before that test, so an exactly stationary starting point is not safely handled by this path. LBFGS and MCSRCH retain SAVE state and shared LB3 parameters; do not interleave independent solves as though this interface were reentrant. Preserve workspace and re-enter with the returned IFLAG. No minimization, gradient comparison or full audit of MCSTEP/BLAS dependencies was executed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision reverse-communication minimizer. N/M are positive default INTEGER; W needs N*(2*M+1)+2*M elements. Initially evaluate F/G and set IFLAG=0. Return 1 requests fresh F/G at X, 2 requests positive DIAG when DIAGCO is true, 0 reports normal completion and negative values report errors. Link the LB2 block-data defaults and keep the state/workspace intact between calls.
procedures.signature: CALL LBFGS(N, M, X, F, G, DIAGCO, DIAG, IPRINT, EPS, XTOL, W, IFLAG)
procedures.usage:
external :: lbfgs, lb2
integer, parameter :: n=2, m=3
integer :: iprint(2), iflag, calls
double precision :: x(n), g(n), diag(n), w(n*(2*m+1)+2*m)
double precision :: f, eps, xtol
logical :: diagco
x=[2.0d0,-1.0d0]
diagco=.false.
iprint=[-1,0]
eps=1.0d-8
xtol=epsilon(1.0d0)
iflag=0
do calls=1,1000
  f=0.5d0*sum(x*x)
  g=x
  call lbfgs(n,m,x,f,g,diagco,diag,iprint,eps,xtol,w,iflag)
  if (iflag <= 0) exit
  if (iflag /= 1) error stop "unexpected reverse-communication request"
end do
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "L-BFGS did not finish normally"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment minimizing a quadratic from an explicitly nonstationary initial point. It uses DIAGCO=false, so no diagonal-request branch is needed. The 1000-call guard is a caller limit, not a library convergence claim. Check an initially stationary point before entering this implementation. Link the complete lbfgs.f object, including LB2 and bundled support routines, with compatible default INTEGER/double precision; archive/block-data retention may require toolchain-specific handling. Saved/shared state prevents safe interleaving of solves.

THOMAS performs the no-pivot forward elimination and back substitution for one real tridiagonal system. It copies the diagonal and right-hand side, so the input arrays are preserved. All four arrays use length N, with AS(1) and CS(N) unused; they are not packed N-1 off-diagonals. N must be positive and all intermediate pivots nonzero. There is no dimension check, singularity status, pivoting, condition estimate or iterative refinement. D2a2a records general real tridiagonal systems, not an SPD-only solver. classifications.notes: The public compact differentiator constructs first- or second-derivative stencils and solves a tridiagonal or cyclic tridiagonal system. The periodic path uses two Thomas solves plus a Sherman-Morrison correction. Its padding treats the first and last samples as a duplicated periodic endpoint; it is not the usual N distinct periodic samples layout. The second argument is the divisor used directly: pass h for the first derivative and h squared for the second, as the CPU heat kernel does. The sixth-order label describes the intended smooth uniform-grid stencil, not a checked observed convergence rate. Nonperiodic constructors take boundary schemes and use the same solver, but their boundary formulas have not been numerically verified. Require enough nodes, positive spacing divisor and nonsingular solves/correction denominator; no status is returned.

local.name: laplace-2D
local.description: Two-dimensional Laplace/Poisson equations on a rectangular grid.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly specifies the equation and prescribed boundary values. Other geometries, Neumann/Robin conditions and convergence behavior are not inferred.

LAPLACE_SOLVE dispatches five-point successive over-relaxation for a rectangular 2D Laplace/Poisson grid, in lexicographic or red-black ordering. Native interior sweeps leave boundary cells unchanged; boundary values and source must already be populated. The grid weights depend on both spacings and the relaxation formula uses their geometric mean. The nonzero source enters the particular stored-source normalization in the update, so callers must derive its scaling rather than pass an arbitrary physical RHS unchanged. The sketch uses zero source to avoid claiming a generic Poisson normalization. The stopping test is maximum iterate change, not a residual norm. The setup local counter K has declaration initialization and therefore SAVE semantics: repeated wrapper calls retain its previous count. Return NSTEPS is not a fresh per-call convergence flag. The separately named SOR9 routine repeats the five-point formula and is not treated as a nine-point method.

args%eps=1d-8; args%maxiter=10000

local.name: Butterworth Filter

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies arbitrary-order Butterworth filtering. Boundary treatment, numerical conditioning at high order and phase behavior have not been independently checked.

The inspected low-pass design prewarps the cutoff with cot(pi*f*dt), assembles first/second-order Butterworth factors and expands their polynomials into coefficient vectors. buttfilt applies a causal recursive linear difference equation with input numerator coefficients b and feedback denominator coefficients a, overwriting samples 0:nt after zero-state initialization. The forward routine omits division by a(0), so it requires a(0)=1; the separate filtfilt implementation divides by a(0) and uses forward/reverse zero-state passes, which is not an equivalent endpoint-transient policy to every other library filtfilt. local.name: Nonstationary AR(1) Markov approximations
local.description: Markov-chain approximations of nonstationary AR(1) processes.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes extensions of Rouwenhorst and Tauchen discretizations. This is transition/state approximation of a stochastic process, not a parameter-estimation routine for arbitrary Markov models.

lcrouwenhorst propagates unconditional standard deviations of a supplied time-varying AR(1), creates a finite symmetric state grid, and recursively constructs Rouwenhorst transition matrices. lctauchen instead forms time-varying grids and Gaussian bin probabilities using ERF. M1a records finite-state discrete stochastic-model construction for simulation, not random path generation or fitted AR parameters. Both assume y(0)=0; rho(1) does not set a stationary initial variance. Output trans(i,j,t) is row-oriented from period t-1 to t, with identical first-period rows. Caller must provide compatible T vectors, N>=2 states, nonzero innovations/variance and valid positive grid scales; no status, input validation or probability/moment check is returned. No chain or approximation-error test was run.

procedures.summary: Public module finite-state AR(1) approximation. Inputs rho(T), sigma_eps(T) use SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307); preallocate output y_grid(N,T), trans(N,N,T). The routine builds transition probabilities and grids; it does not draw observations.
procedures.usage:
use mod_lcrouwenhorst, only: lcrouwenhorst
integer, parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(15,307),n=5,t=4
real(dp) :: rho(t),sigma_eps(t),grid(n,t),transition(n,n,t)
rho=0.8_dp; sigma_eps=0.1_dp
call lcrouwenhorst(rho,sigma_eps,grid,transition)
! Check nonnegativity, row sums and model moments independently.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use at least two states and one period with compatible shapes; avoid zero standard deviations in formulas that divide by sigma. The first grid represents a process starting from zero, not stationary initialization. The returned chain is an approximation to the continuous-valued AR process; neither transition probabilities nor moments were checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public alternative using normal-bin probabilities and omega(T) range multipliers. Uses the same row/time indexing and preallocated grid/transition outputs; positive sigma_eps and omega are required.
procedures.signature: CALL lctauchen(rho, sigma_eps, omega, y_grid, trans)

local.name: acepack
local.description: R interfaces to Fortran ACE and AVAS regression-transformation algorithms.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the original Fortran kernels and modifications for double-precision R use. The relative advantages described for ACE/AVAS are not independently reproduced here.

The selected SUPSMU entry smooths ordered weighted observations with running local linear fits. Positive module SPAN selects the fixed-span path; zero invokes candidate spans, cross-validation residual smoothing and interpolated locally selected spans. It is an EDA smoother, not the complete ACE/AVAS transformation estimator. The sketch explicitly uses IPER=1 and fixed SPAN=0.5: the periodic branch in SMOOTH reads X(J) before correcting a negative wrapped index and needs repair/bounds checking before use. SUPSMU has no status output, divides by total weight for constant x and accesses quartile indices, so supply sufficiently many finite sorted data and positive total weights. Module control state is shared; no accuracy or smoothing-selection experiment was performed. SMOOTH also combines J<N with X(J+1)<=X(J) in a logical expression: Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation, so tied terminal abscissae can expose X(N+1). The sketch uses strictly increasing x; this is not a fix or bounds-safety proof.

procedures.summary: External double-precision weighted smoother controlled by the ACEDATA module. This sketch selects a nonperiodic fixed span.
procedures.usage:
use acedata, only: span
integer, parameter :: n=20
integer :: i
double precision :: x(n),y(n),w(n),smo(n),scratch(n,7)
external :: supsmu
do i=1,n
  x(i)=dble(i); y(i)=x(i)**2
enddo
w=1.0d0; span=0.5d0
call supsmu(n,x,y,w,1,smo,scratch)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use the selected IPER=1 branch; the periodic branch has an index-order finding recorded here. Choose n large enough for the requested smoothing window; no input checks protect short arrays. Module controls persist across calls. No residual, cross-validation or bounds-checking run was performed. Supply strictly increasing abscissae; the tied-abscissa loop also needs bounds review.

local.name: ASURV
local.description: Survival-analysis methods for censored data with a Fortran backend and Python interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README lists Kaplan-Meier estimation, two-sample tests, correlations and censored regressions. The broad mapping does not validate assumptions or every method/configuration in the suite.

PLESTM forms a product-limit survival estimator from sorted uncensored/censored arrays, accumulates pointwise standard-error terms, and computes a mean and its error. The implementation first converts largest censored observations to detections until the tail is uncensored, mutating U, NU and NC and reporting ICHANGE/NCHANGE. This is an explicit tail convention, not an assumption-free estimate of an unidentified unrestricted mean. NTOT-sized arrays need spare space for moved observations; all-censored input is unsafe because U(NU) is read before NU is checked. Tied/small samples also expose loops reading U(I+K) before a bound test, and Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation. No recoverable status output certifies valid inputs. Higher-level ASURV wrappers handle censoring direction/data transformation separately. Review covers the product-limit implementation and tail conventions, not the complete interactive package or validation of survival inference.

procedures.summary: External REAL*8 survival-estimator kernel with mutable detection/censor counts and no INFO argument.
procedures.usage:
external :: PLESTM
! Prepare sorted transformed U/C arrays of length NTOT, NU>=1, NU+NC=NTOT.
! S/V are REAL*8 arrays; L is integer workspace, all NTOT entries.
! Preserve original data/counts and review the recorded tie/boundary issues first.
call PLESTM(u,c,nu,nc,s,v,ntot,mean,mean_error,ichange,nchange,ranks)
! Check ICHANGE/NCHANGE before interpreting a mean based on tail conversions.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. A post-validation interface fragment, not a statistically checked survival example. Censoring direction must match the higher-level ASURV transformations. Repair/validate all-censored, tied-tail and small-sample bounds before use. No survival curve, mean or standard error was tested.

local.name: BGW
local.description: R interfaces to Fortran Bunch-Gay-Welsch statistical-estimation algorithms.

DESCRIPTION documents current maximum-likelihood estimation and a statistical-structure-aware trust-region approach. Nonlinear least squares and generalized method-of-moments are described as possible extensions, not assumed current R interfaces.

The selected DRGLG entry performs unconstrained NL2SOL-like iterations for an objective composed from model values R and their first derivatives DR, dispatching to DG7LIT_M and QR/curvature-update machinery. In this R-package revision the linked RHO is specifically weighted/unweighted negative log probability, with derivatives -1/R and 1/R**2; it is not a freely supplied RHO callback argument or arbitrary least-squares objective by default. The caller supplies model values/Jacobians at reverse-communication requests and must interpret IV(1) according to the package protocol, including diagnostic requests. Require positive finite model probabilities and valid initialized work/state arrays. The BIND(C) interface passes LRHOI/LRHOR by VALUE while most scalars are by reference: an explicit matching interface is essential. This is driver dispatch/source structure, not a full audit of all trust-region, covariance or diagnostic kernels or a maximum-likelihood accuracy check.

local.name: SplitMix64 Fortran
local.description: Fortran 2008 implementation of the SplitMix64 generator.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies the generator and reference C implementation. Arithmetic portability, seeding and stream properties have not been checked for this translation.

splitmix64_next adds the fixed golden-ratio increment to a local copy of its INTENT(IN) seed, applies two XOR-shift/multiply mixers and a final XOR shift, returning an INT64 bit-pattern harvest. The caller seed is unchanged: calling repeatedly with the same seed repeats the same output. Assigning harvest back as the next seed instead iterates a different map from the usual SplitMix counter progression. L6a21 records the generator mixing step rather than claiming an automatically advancing stream or a real-valued uniform API. The BOZ constants are passed through TRANSFER, and signed integer addition/multiplication still assumes intended wrapping. No bitstream/reference or portability test was run.

procedures.summary: Public pure elemental INT64 function of an INTENT(IN) seed. Despite the name next, the input seed is not advanced. This sketch demonstrates one mixing call only, not a complete repeated-draw driver.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: int64
use pkg_splitmix64, only: splitmix64_next
integer(int64) :: seed, harvest
seed = 123_int64
harvest = splitmix64_next(seed)
! seed remains 123; repeated calls with it repeat harvest.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile the parent module before its submodule. For a standard successive SplitMix sequence, manage the additive counter progression separately with explicitly supported modular arithmetic; do not assume this function updates it or that seed=harvest reproduces that progression. TRANSFER with BOZ source and integer wrapping need compiler support. No period or distribution claim was verified.

local.name: xorshift64* Fortran
local.description: Fortran implementation of xorshift64* using signed-integer representation workarounds.

classifications.notes: The README describes a multiword signed-integer workaround for unsigned arithmetic. Correct equivalence to the reference algorithm and behavior across compilers remain unverified.

RandomNumberGenerator%random_uniform dispatches to a xorshift64star state update using shifts 12,25,27 and an explicit base-2**16 multiplication modulo 2**64. It then assembles a floating-point fraction from the four words. L6a21 records uniform-output sampling; state must be seeded to a nonzero C_INT64_T bit pattern, since zero is absorbing. Scalar and rank-one through rank-three wrappers share this state. Conversion to C_DOUBLE can round a high unsigned fraction to 1, despite the intended [0,1) range; callers must not assume a strict upper bound. The OpenMP critical region serializes scalar draws but does not establish independent parallel streams. No sequence, endpoint or reference comparison was run.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound generic returning a scalar or array of C_DOUBLE values. The sketch selects a scalar and constructs a nonzero explicit seed. Scalar generation updates state inside an OpenMP critical region when enabled.
procedures.usage:
use precision, only: dp, di
use random, only: RandomNumberGenerator
type(RandomNumberGenerator) :: generator
real(dp) :: u
generator = RandomNumberGenerator(123456_di)
call generator%random_uniform(u)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile precision before random. Require a nonzero seed. Floating-point conversion does not enforce u<1; range-sensitive consumers need endpoint handling. The private kernel uses limb multiplication rather than signed 64-bit multiply overflow, but no integer/reference equivalence or parallel reproducibility test was executed.

classifications.notes: The public random_normal generic uses the Box-Muller transform of two uniform draws, returning one sine component and saving the cosine component. This supports normal random-variate generation L6a14. A SAVE cache/has_cache belongs to the procedure, not each RandomNumberGenerator; interleaving two objects can return a cached value derived from the other object, and reseeding an object does not clear it. OpenMP marks the cache threadprivate, not per object. LOG(u(1)) is unguarded for a zero uniform output. This source mapping records the implemented transform and lifecycle limits, not independent streams or a verified normal law. No sample was run.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound generic; this card shows the scalar C_DOUBLE output. Each pair uses Box-Muller and a procedure-level saved second value. Do not assume the generator state alone fully captures subsequent normal outputs.
procedures.usage:
use precision, only: dp, di
use random, only: RandomNumberGenerator
type(RandomNumberGenerator) :: generator
real(dp) :: z
generator = RandomNumberGenerator(123456_di)
call generator%random_normal(z)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This single-object first-call sketch does not fix the shared-cache behavior. LOG has no zero-endpoint guard, and the cached variate survives object reseeding. Resolve those requirements before relying on per-object reproducibility, independent streams or finite output. No goodness-of-fit or moment check was run.

local.name: LAPACK
local.description: Reference Fortran numerical linear algebra library with BLAS and language interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the broad reference library and Make/CMake builds. This upstream repository is distinct from the selected perazz/fortran-lapack wrapper; individual routine mappings and build configurations remain to be reviewed here.

The inspected DGESV driver solves a general real dense square system with one or more right-hand sides. It checks dimensions, dispatches LU factorization with partial pivoting to DGETRF and solves through DGETRS only if factorization reports success. A is overwritten by LU factors and B by the solution; positive INFO reports an exactly zero pivot. D2a1 is the general-system class. This source review covers the driver interface and dispatch, not an audit of every BLAS/LAPACK kernel or vendor implementation. It does not establish conditioning, error bounds, inverse formation, sparse support or numerical accuracy by execution.

procedures.summary: External double-precision dense linear-system driver. A(LDA,N) is overwritten by factors, B(LDB,NRHS) by solutions, and IPIV(N) records row pivots. Check INFO before using the solution. Link a compatible LAPACK/BLAS library; this source file alone is insufficient.
procedures.signature: CALL DGESV(N, NRHS, A, LDA, IPIV, B, LDB, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgesv
integer :: ipiv(2), info
double precision :: a(2,2), b(2,1)
a = reshape([3.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
b(:,1) = [9.0d0, 8.0d0]
call dgesv(2, 1, a, 2, ipiv, b, 2, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGESV failed"
! The solution is now in b(:,1).
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only, not a checked driver. Use a double-precision/integer ABI compatible with the linked LAPACK build; a vendor ILP64 build needs matching integer arguments. Preserve input copies if residuals or the original matrix are needed. INFO=0 is not a condition-number or accuracy estimate. No compilation, residual calculation or solver comparison was performed.

classifications.notes: The inspected real DGELS driver chooses QR or LQ factorization by matrix shape and applies orthogonal transformations and triangular solves for unconstrained least squares or minimum-norm underdetermined solves. For TRANS=N and M>=N, the reviewed path forms Q-transpose B and solves with R. The interface assumes full rank; positive INFO detects exactly zero triangular diagonals, not reliable numerical rank or near-singularity. D9a1 records the unconstrained L2 solution scope. Workspace queries and scaling are visible in the driver. This review does not certify all dependency kernels, rank-deficient methods, constrained least squares or runtime accuracy.

procedures.summary: External full-rank real least-squares/minimum-norm driver. TRANS selects A or its transpose. A and B are overwritten; B needs at least MAX(1,M,N) rows even when the input right-hand side is shorter. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 before allocating the working buffer, then check INFO after the solve.
procedures.signature: CALL DGELS(TRANS, M, N, NRHS, A, LDA, B, LDB, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgels
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(3,2), b(3,1), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a(:,1) = 1.0d0
a(:,2) = [0.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0]
b(:,1) = [1.0d0, 2.0d0, 2.0d0]
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS failed"
! For this M>=N case, b(1:2,1) holds the fitted coefficients.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Link compatible LAPACK and BLAS and match the integer/real ABI. The example uses the full-rank overdetermined TRANS=N branch; it is not a rank-revealing solver demonstration. Preserve original A/B for an independent residual check. Neither the fit nor any underdetermined branch was run for this catalog.

classifications.notes: The inspected DSYEV driver computes ordinary eigenvalues of a real symmetric dense matrix, optionally eigenvectors. It reads the selected triangle, reduces through DSYTRD and dispatches eigenvalues-only work to DSTERF or the vector path through DORGTR and DSTEQR; optional scaling is undone on the eigenvalues. D4a1 is the real-symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem scope. This is not a generalized, complex, nonsymmetric or subset-eigensolver mapping. The driver exposes workspace-query and convergence status, but no eigenpair residual, orthogonality check or audit of all lower-level kernels was performed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision symmetric eigensolver. JOBZ selects values alone or values plus vectors; UPLO selects the stored triangle. Eigenvalues are returned in ascending order. A is overwritten, holding eigenvectors on a successful JOBZ=V call. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 and check INFO.
procedures.signature: CALL DSYEV(JOBZ, UPLO, N, A, LDA, W, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dsyev
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(2,2), w(2), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a = reshape([2.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
call dsyev("V", "U", 2, a, 2, w, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DSYEV query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dsyev("V", "U", 2, a, 2, w, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DSYEV failed"
! w contains eigenvalues; columns of a contain eigenvectors.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Match the linked LAPACK/BLAS ABI and use only the selected triangle as input. Keep the original matrix for independent eigenpair-residual and orthogonality checks; INFO=0 alone is not such a check. Neither the sample eigenproblem nor the author test suite was run.

local.name: HSSPACK
local.description: HSS-based algorithms for tridiagonal eigenproblems, bidiagonal SVD and divide-and-conquer problems.

classifications.notes: The short README specifies specialized matrix forms and hierarchically semiseparable techniques. These component algorithms are not advertised as unrestricted dense eigensolver/SVD replacements.
The short README specifies specialized matrix forms and hierarchically semiseparable techniques. These component algorithms are not advertised as unrestricted dense eigensolver/SVD replacements.

HSSCHOLSOLVER solves a real dense symmetric positive-definite system through an approximate hierarchical semiseparable Cholesky representation, optionally refined by preconditioned CG. The caller supplies a dense matrix, block/rank/compression controls and one RHS vector, despite comments mentioning multiple RHSs. RS=S selects deterministic SVD compression and RS=R randomized compression; WPCG=N uses the approximate direct solve, Y the iterative refinement path. Selected construction code compresses tree blocks and applies local Cholesky/orthogonal transformations; SOLVECHOLSVD traverses the factor tree and applies triangular solves. INFO validates option flags but is not propagated from lower-level factorization/convergence/allocation failures (some allocation exits retain INFO=0). Thus INFO=0 is not a numerical solve certificate. Input A is copied internally and B overwritten; preserve original RHS and check a residual. Review covers the driver and selected construction/solve tree paths, not all low-rank kernels or an accuracy/scaling guarantee.

procedures.summary: External dense SPD hierarchical approximate Cholesky/optional-PCG driver with one RHS.
procedures.usage:
external :: HssCholSolver
integer :: n,ni,rank_cap,oversampling,maxit,info
double precision :: tol,tau
! Allocate/initialize DOUBLE PRECISION A(N,N), RHS(N), and preserve copies.
! Use a sufficiently sized SPD matrix with compressible off-diagonal blocks.
ni=20; rank_cap=10; oversampling=5; maxit=30; tol=1d-8; tau=1d-12
call HssCholSolver("S","N",a,n,rhs,ni,tol,rank_cap,oversampling,tau,maxit,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "invalid HSS options"
! Independently validate the returned solution residual against original A/RHS.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-allocation fragment using author-style block/rank controls. Link the complete HSSPACK/BLAS/LAPACK build; adapt controls to actual matrix size and structure. INFO does not carry all numerical failures or establish residual accuracy. No SPD solve, compression, randomized or PCG case was run.

classifications.notes: DHSSMM compresses a dense square real A into a hierarchical semiseparable representation, then traverses its low-rank factor tree to overwrite dense B with approximate A*B in column panels. FASTHSSMM applies upward/downward tree products with dense block multiplications. The wrapper assumes LDA=M=N and needs valid block/rank and panel sizes; this is not a general rectangular matrix product. The selected wrapper has concrete limitations: INFO is never assigned, the remainder-panel branch slices B rows instead of columns, and multiplication TIME(2) subtracts clocks in reverse order. The sketch therefore restricts K to a positive multiple of NCOL and does not interpret INFO or timing as validation. Compression tolerance controls internal approximations, not an independently measured product error. Review covers construction/product dispatch and selected tree multiply paths; it does not certify every compression kernel or OpenMP variant.

procedures.summary: External panel-wise approximate dense product through HSS compression, with restricted safe panel shape.
procedures.usage:
external :: DHSSMM
integer :: n,k,panel,ni,rank_cap,info
double precision :: tol,times(2)
! Allocate/initialize A(N,N), B(N,K), preserve copies, and choose N/block sizes.
panel=20; k=40; ni=20; rank_cap=10; tol=1d-8; info=-999
! B must already be allocated with K=40 columns; K is a multiple of PANEL.
call DHSSMM(a,n,n,n,b,n,k,tol,rank_cap,ni,panel,times,info)
! INFO is not assigned, and TIMES(2) is reversed; validate A*B independently.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-allocation fragment only. Use a square matrix and a positive panel size dividing K to avoid the reviewed remainder-slice defect. Build all HSSPACK dependencies; do not rely on unassigned INFO or the reversed timing. No product, compression error, remainder case or timing was tested.

local.name: Lanczos Iterator
local.description: Matrix-free Lanczos methods for low-lying real-symmetric or complex-Hermitian eigenpairs.

classifications.notes: The README requires a user-supplied matrix-vector product and describes residual-based polishing. Its maximal-precision and robustness claims have not been independently reproduced.

rs_lanczos creates real vector views over output columns and invokes the iterator sequentially for the lowest requested eigenpairs of a matrix supplied by callback. The inspected core performs a three-term Lanczos update with orthogonalization, reduces to a tridiagonal problem and dispatches Ritz extraction/polishing. D4a1 records real-symmetric ordinary eigenproblems, not nonsymmetric/generalized solvers. Callback ADD controls overwrite versus accumulation and must be honored. The output named variance is filled by residual using vector_norm, so it is a residual norm rather than a squared variance. There is no public success flag; maxstep does not bound all later polishing work. Saved RNG/recurrence state prevents assuming reentrancy. The wrapper seed packing is normalized to a valid odd final seed by vector_random_fill before LAPACK use. Restart/range mode and complex variants are outside the usage sketch. No eigenpair or independent residual was computed.

procedures.summary: External real-symmetric matrix-free eigensolver. Supply double-precision eval(nevec), evec(n,nevec), residual-norm output variance(nevec), resolution, callback and controls. The public DHSVD2 module procedure performs a two-by-two real hyperbolic singular-value transformation, using a signature J with entries +/-1. local.description: C and Python interfaces to Fortran DL-FIND geometry optimization.

classifications.notes: The README documents a callback-driven geometry-optimization backend and examples with external electronic-structure code. Its interface is distinct from a standalone implementation of every DL-FIND optimization method.

classifications.notes: The README architecture diagrams separate user equations/boundaries, semidiscretization and DASSL integration. The entry does not imply that arbitrary PDEs are solved without user callbacks or an appropriate time integrator.

DRAW_JU generates correlation-matrix draws using sequential beta-distributed partial correlations and the Joe construction. The output stores the strict lower-triangle correlations in row-by-row order (2,1),(3,1),(3,2),(4,1),(4,2),(4,3),..., with unit diagonal implicit; NUMCORRGROUP must equal P*(P-1)/2. The public update_factor_normal component draws latent Gaussian factor scores conditional on the supplied loadings, dedicated-factor assignments, idiosyncratic precisions and factor covariance distribution. TrilinosEigenSolver exposes A*x=lambda*x without an M operator through Anasazi::BasicEigenproblem. Setup requires NumEV, Solver Type and a matching named solver sublist; initial vectors are randomized. The selected general real interface does not set a Hermitian flag, so no symmetric specialization is inferred. Eigenvalues are written as alternating real/imaginary C_DOUBLE entries, with C_INT eigenindex encoding and a TpetraMultiVector for vectors. The integer function result is the returned value count; use %converged() separately and check independent residuals. local.name: Fortran Rationals
local.description: Rational-number arithmetic with checked finite-width integer representation.

classifications.notes: The README specifies int64 numerators/denominators and stopping on invalid arithmetic or overflow. Exact arithmetic within representable limits is not arbitrary-precision unbounded arithmetic.

The rational type stores reduced INT64 numerator/denominator pairs with positive denominator. The selected integer constructors simplify with Euclidean GCF, reject zero denominators and the most-negative integer, and normalize signs. Rational addition cancels denominator common factors before checked integer products/sums; multiplication cancels cross factors before multiplying. These are exact finite-width rational operations, not arbitrary precision. Error paths use ERROR STOP and some representable final results can still encounter finite intermediate limits; this review does not prove completeness of overflow handling across every operator. Other intrinsic overloads, matrices, random rational generation and formatted I/O are outside this selected arithmetic review.

procedures.summary: Public generic integer-pair constructor; the selected overload takes two INT64 arguments. Private components are exposed through get_num/get_den queries.

use iso_fortran_env, only: int64
use rationals, only: rational, operator(+), operator(*)
type(rational) :: a,b,c
integer(int64) :: numerator, denominator
a=rational(1_int64,3_int64)
b=rational(1_int64,6_int64)
c=a+b
numerator=c%get_num()
denominator=c%get_den()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The sketch selects the INT64 constructor and public generic operators. Arithmetic is bounded by finite integer representation; zero denominators and checked overflows terminate the process. No exact-result or overflow-boundary tests were run.

Public rational multiplication operator with cross-factor cancellation; private implementation names are not separate user APIs.

classifications.notes: The REAL64 rational constructor iterates continued-fraction convergents until conversion back to REAL64 equals the original absolute input, the fractional remainder vanishes, or the next convergent/reciprocal exceeds the finite INT64 bounds. It then restores the sign. Consequently this is a real-to-fraction conversion/approximation, not a promise of representing the exact binary rational or the originally intended decimal. If no round-tripping convergent fits, the last fitting convergent is retained. Nonfinite/out-of-range input reaches ERROR STOP. The reverse REAL overload divides the stored integer components in REAL64 and rounds normally. No round-trip or best-approximation experiment was performed.

classifications.notes: The public integer gcf and lcm generics expose Euclidean greatest-common-factor calculation and divide-before-checked-multiply least-common-multiple calculation. GCF normalizes with ABS and defines zero cases, including gcf(0,0)=0; LCM returns zero if either input is zero. INT32 overloads compute via INT64 and reject results exceeding INT32. The direct INT64 GCF/LCM path applies ABS without guarding the most-negative representable INT64 input, which is excluded from this mapping usage. B is the available GAMS number-theory leaf; this is not primality or factorization software. No integer-result or boundary tests were run.

local.name: HDMod
local.description: Fortran hyper-dual-number arithmetic and calculations.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies hyper-dual-number calculations. Individual derivative interfaces, supported operations and numerical behavior need further source review; no complete automatic-differentiation framework is inferred.

The hyperdual type stores value, two first-direction components and a mixed component. The selected hdual constructor copies all four seeds. hdexp and hdsin propagate first derivatives and the mixed second derivative by chain-rule formulas, including the incoming mixed seed. For a univariate x seeded as (x,1,1,0), dx1 and dx2 represent the first derivative and dx1x2 the second derivative of the selected smooth expression. This is operator/function-based automatic differentiation, not a finite-difference step-size method or a full Hessian driver. Only the scalar constructor, exponential and sine paths were inspected; thousands of other overloads, branch logic and nonsmooth/domain behavior are outside this review. Floating-point errors/overflow remain and no derivative check was run.

local.name: compare
local.description: Tolerance-based comparisons of real and complex numbers.

classifications.notes: The README describes absolute differences and an optional/default tolerance. Its approximate relations are not assumed to have all equivalence/order properties of exact arithmetic.

The selected eq generic compares absolute differences with a tolerance, including default-real scalars, REAL64 scalars, default complex scalars and real arrays. local.name: fortran-approx
local.description: Absolute and absolute-plus-relative floating-point comparison interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README documents elemental comparisons, precision variants and default tolerances. Choosing a tolerance remains application-dependent; approximate equality is not a certified error bound.

The public elemental aeq and haeq generics implement absolute tolerance abs(a-b)<=tol and hybrid tolerance abs(a-b)<=atol+rtol*max(abs(a),abs(b)). Defaults are 1e-10 in each supported real kind. Array calls return elementwise logical masks, unlike the scalar array-reduction behavior of tcanich/compare. Explicit tolerances must match the argument kind; haeq exposes two-argument default or four-argument explicit forms. Negative tolerances, NaNs/infinities and subtraction/scaled-threshold overflow are not specially handled, so the mapping/sketch is limited to finite ordinary-range values and nonnegative tolerances. local.name: Powell optimization archive
local.description: Archive of M. J. D. Powell Fortran 77 optimization software.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly says these implementations are no longer maintained and directs users to PRIMA for modernized reference implementations. This entry describes the archive without asserting current compiler readiness.

BOBYQA performs local derivative-free minimization of a smooth objective subject to simple bounds, using interpolating quadratic models and bounded trust-region subproblems. The reviewed wrapper partitions workspace, checks interpolation-count/bound-spacing restrictions and adjusts the starting point near bounds; BOBYQB dispatches model steps and objective evaluations. The model gradient is internal and does not mean the caller supplies derivatives. Require N>=2, N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)(N+2)/2, positive ordered radii and each bound interval at least twice RHOBEG. This original interface returns the best sampled variables but no explicit convergence flag or objective output argument. Printed termination reasons, independent objective/feasibility checks and evaluation-budget exhaustion must be distinguished; RHOEND is a radius target, not a solution-error certificate. This is a local constrained method, not global optimization.

call bobyqa(n,npt,x,xl,xu,0.5d0,1d-6,1,500,w)
! Re-evaluate the objective and bound feasibility; no status code is returned.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build the complete BOBYQA folder with a matching custom CALFUN instead of its supplied problem callback. Do not combine unrelated solver-folder callbacks/symbols blindly. No minimum, termination reason, budget or bound residual was tested.

classifications.notes: COBYLA minimizes an objective subject to nonlinear inequalities using simplex interpolation of objective/constraint values and native linearized trust-region subproblems. The caller supplies CALCFC values with feasible constraints CON>=0; it supplies neither objective nor constraint derivatives. G2h3b1a records the smooth general nonlinear-constraint/no-derivative scope, with zero equality constraints in this selected interface. Equalities are not separate inputs and tight paired inequalities need independent care. Unlike the other reviewed Powell folders, this copy has no IMPLICIT REAL*8 declaration and its Makefile does not promote REAL, so the reviewed default build uses default-real arrays and radii. MAXFUN is an input evaluation limit overwritten with evaluations used. There is no returned convergence code, and small final simplex radius does not guarantee feasibility or an accurate optimum.

procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Match the actual build precision in the driver, all solver files and CALCFC. Do not pass DOUBLE PRECISION solely because other Powell folders use it. No constrained optimum, precision-promoted build or feasibility tolerance was run.

classifications.notes: LINCOA performs local derivative-free minimization of a smooth objective with linear inequalities, building quadratic interpolation models and solving linearly constrained model trust subproblems. Columns A(:,J) are constraint normals for A(:,J) dot X<=B(J). The wrapper normalizes constraints and, if the initial point violates one, increases its internal normalized right-hand side to admit that point; the input B array itself is not overwritten by this adjustment. A feasible initial point is therefore important if the original feasible region must be preserved. Model-improvement objective calls may be infeasible; the incoming sign of F is a feasibility indicator before CALFUN overwrites it. Require nonzero constraint normals, valid N/NPT/radii and sufficient budget/workspace. W(1) and W(2) return objective and evaluation-count information after the normal algorithm; invalid-input early returns need separate handling and there is no explicit status code. It is neither linear programming nor a global optimum certificate.

procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The initial point here satisfies the stored inequality. The internal relaxation on other starting points can change the problem being solved. Use the complete matching LINCOA folder and replace its example callback; no feasibility, model step or optimum was tested.

classifications.notes: NEWUOA minimizes a smooth unconstrained multivariate function from a supplied initial point without user derivatives. It forms quadratic interpolation models with least-change Hessian updates and calls a truncated-CG trust-region model solver. N must be at least two, NPT must lie in the documented interpolation range, and both radii must be positive with RHOEND<=RHOBEG. This original entry uses a globally linked CALFUN symbol and a caller-sized double-precision workspace, changes X and reports progress through printing rather than a returned convergence status. The callback must be defined on trial points outside any intended box because no bounds are enforced. This mapping records the native local search/dispatch and model step, not a guarantee that RHOEND measures actual solution error or that a global minimum is found.

classifications.notes: GETMIN is the documented TOLMIN entry for a differentiable objective with linear equalities/inequalities and simple bounds. The caller supplies FGCALC objective and first derivatives; the solver maintains active constraints, seeks feasibility, uses line searches and tests the projected first-order/KKT residual against ACC. Constraint normals occupy columns; the first MEQ constraints are equalities and subsequent constraints use A(:,J) dot X<=B(J). Fixed variables can use equal lower/upper bounds. INFO is an input evaluation limit (zero means no imposed limit) and an output reason: 1 is the normal feasibility/first-order stop, while 2/3 indicate stalled feasible progress and 4 through 8 report invalid/inconsistent constraints or budget exhaustion. Return is not a second-order or global optimality certificate. Review covers the public contract, feasibility/minimization dispatch and native first-order stopping path, not every degeneracy/line-search dependency.

The external MT1 routine solves a binary single-capacity profit-maximizing knapsack through greedy initialization, integer upper bounds, branching and backtracking. CHMT1 checks selected admissibility conditions when JCK=1: at least two items, positive integer profits/weights/capacity, every weight <= capacity, total weight > capacity and nonincreasing profit/weight ratios. It is not a wrapper that sorts arbitrary inputs or handles the all-items-fit case. All eight arrays need N+1 elements; sentinel slots P(N+1),W(N+1) are overwritten despite a blanket unchanged-input comment. Integer products/sums and default-REAL ratio/bound arithmetic can overflow or lose precision; no large-instance robustness or optimality experiment was run. This mapping is the selected MT1 path, not every MT2/generalized/multiple knapsack algorithm.

classifications.notes: MTP minimizes the number of equal-capacity bins through a packing heuristic, lower bounds, reduction and ENUMER branch-and-bound, then reconstructs original item assignments. BACK=-1 requests unrestricted enumeration while nonnegative values bound backtracking and may return a heuristic solution. Z is the achieved bin count, LB a lower bound, XSTAR the item-to-bin assignment; compare bounds before claiming optimality. local.name: Singular surface operators
local.description: Nystrom discretization of weakly singular integral operators on surfaces.

classifications.notes: The README identifies single/double-layer potentials and the associated discretization paper. Operator discretization is not taken as evidence of a complete general integral-equation solver.

CADAPTRI adaptively integrates a complex-valued callback over a planar triangle. It compares a parent integral against the sum over four midpoint subtriangles, accepts the parent when the absolute difference is below EPS, otherwise recursively processes children through an explicit stack. The one-triangle kernel maps a hardcoded 82-node rule by an affine transformation and absolute Jacobian determinant. Header claims of a 60-point rule and approximately 30 digits are not accepted as precision evidence; the implementation uses double precision. EPS is a local parent/children comparison, not an apportioned bound on accumulated global error. NQUAD adds 79 per accepted parent and is inconsistent with the 82-node kernel and refinement evaluations, so it is not an actual function-evaluation counter. IER=4/16 report stack/depth exhaustion and partial VAL must not be treated as a complete integral. The source file begins with a debugging main; extract the documented library section to avoid duplicate main programs. Review covers this planar adaptive kernel, not the full singular surface-operator solver.

The public CONJUGATE_GRADIENT%SOLVE binding implements unpreconditioned CG for an attached real linear operator, including the sparse stencil operators used by this finite-volume framework. The native recurrence updates residual, search direction and the iterate using inherited matrix actions and scalar products. The operator must be symmetric positive definite in the actual pairing; the code does not verify symmetry/positivity, and its tiny-PAP guard checks magnitude rather than positive curvature. The stopping threshold is TOLERANCE*(1+NORM(RHS)); ACHIEVED reports a residual norm, but return can also follow a tiny denominator or exhausted iteration budget. There is no separate reason/status output. Affine constants from an attached operation must be moved to the RHS consistently. This mapping records sparse symmetric solver usage, not a sparse storage-format API or a guarantee for nonsymmetric/indefinite systems.

classifications.notes: The public GMRES%SOLVE binding implements restarted real GMRES for attached general linear actions, including sparse finite-volume stencils. It uses native Arnoldi orthogonalization, Givens rotations, triangular back substitution and correction updates. RESTART is the Krylov dimension, while MAX_ITERATIONS bounds outer restart cycles rather than the total number of matrix actions. On an estimated-tolerance exit the true residual norm is recomputed before returning, but an exhausted final cycle can leave an estimate as ACHIEVED. Zero MAX_ITERATIONS can leave that output undefined. The radius/breakdown branch can still reach division by a zero triangular diagonal; return has no dedicated failure/status code. Require positive tolerances, sensible dimensions, initialized attachment and explicit affine-RHS handling. This is a general sparse/operator solver mapping, not a rank-deficient least-squares solver or automatically preconditioned algorithm.

No positive-definiteness, unbiased weighted-estimator or missing-value claim is made; no covariance was checked by execution.

classifications.notes: GRID1D_LOCATE performs binary interval search on an ascending grid, and GRID1D_INTERP returns the local linear weight W=(X-GRID(KI))/(GRID(KI+1)-GRID(KI)). Use at least two strictly increasing finite nodes and call the weight routine only after successful location. KI is unassigned on an out-of-range location failure. Distinct nodes avoid a zero denominator. Shared module LOCATED state means even this locator is not a pure/reentrant service. No interpolation or endpoint behavior was run.

local.name: FERRE
local.description: Parameter fitting by interpolation in tabulated model grids and chi-squared matching.

classifications.notes: The README requires model predictions supplied as an array and describes covariance outputs. Validity of inferred parameter errors and coverage outside the supplied model grid are not established.

LIN performs multilinear interpolation of vector-valued responses on a tensor-product parameter grid. It converts normalized parameter coordinates into grid indices, loads 2**NDIM neighboring response vectors from the shared in-memory array or direct-access file and repeatedly interpolates along configured parameter axes. This supports multivariate gridded interpolation, not scattered interpolation or a fit of model parameters. The short routine depends on fully initialized SHARE dimensions, strides, axis/order maps and grid/file data. It has no local clipping or endpoint correction: at p=1 its corner indexing can request a neighbor past the final grid cell, so callers must follow the enclosing package coordinate conventions and verify boundaries. The scratch response array grows exponentially with dimension. SHARE sets DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(6) in this pin, despite historical double-precision comments elsewhere; use the actual module kind. No shape/range/status validation is returned by LIN.

classifications.notes: The public POLY_FIT wrapper forms powers of input abscissae and inverse-variance weights, then dispatches the bundled incremental least-squares factorization and coefficient backsolve for a polynomial approximation. The intended polynomial-fitting mapping is supported by this construction and the native factorization/backsolve components, but the wrapper has an important dimension mismatch: XROW has N+1 entries, while STARTUP(N+1,.TRUE.) sets NCOL=N+2 and INCLUD loops through NCOL. This can access beyond XROW and must be repaired/validated before relying on results. INFO from SING is subsequently overwritten by REGCF, so it is not a complete record of every intermediate issue. Saved module factorization arrays also make independent concurrent fits unsafe. DP is imported from SHARE and requests six decimal digits at this pin; power-basis conditioning and uncertainty interpretations are not verified.

classifications.notes: The public MINIM routine implements an adapted Nelder-Mead simplex search for FERRE model matching. It creates a simplex from nonzero parameter steps, evaluates the package OBJFUN, and applies reflection, expansion and contraction/shrink logic without requiring user derivatives or a smoothness test. G1b2 records this local general-function minimization scope, not a global optimizer. This adaptation is coupled to SHARE and model/observation arrays: FUNC is the returned objective value, not a callback argument, despite older generic FUNCTN comments. NOP, the active parameter mapping and all array/module dimensions must agree. Stopping uses dispersion of simplex objective values at configured intervals; small dispersion alone does not establish stationarity or parameter error.
