local.name: Mathematics of Arrays for Fortran
local.description: Array take/drop and vector offset operations in a modern Fortran module library.

classifications.notes: The README lists scalar take/drop on vectors and a gamma offset function as implemented. The gamma name here concerns array indexing, not the special Gamma function; a complete array algebra is not inferred.

The Fypp-generated public moa_take/moa_drop generics select vector sections by signed counts and return POINTER views, not allocated copies. Take with a positive count selects the prefix and negative count the suffix; take zero yields an empty section. Positive drop selects the remainder after removing a prefix. The inspected nonpositive drop branch uses vec(:(n+sigma-1)), an off-by-one discrepancy: drop zero removes one element and negative drop removes one extra trailing element. The sketch therefore uses only positive drop. Counts with abs(sigma)>SIZE(vec) print a diagnostic and return a disassociated pointer; minimum-integer ABS overflow is unchecked. Actual vectors must be persistent TARGET objects if the returned pointer is retained. This is vector section service (D1a11), not a mathematical gamma function or general array algebra audit.

procedures.summary: Public generic with Fypp-generated integer-count/integer-or-real vector overloads. Returns a pointer alias into the argument, with unit lower bound for the selected section.
procedures.usage:
use mod_prec, only: di, dd
use moa, only: moa_take, moa_drop
real(dd), target :: vec(4)
real(dd), pointer :: prefix(:), remainder(:)
vec=[1.0_dd,2.0_dd,3.0_dd,4.0_dd]
prefix=>moa_take(2_di,vec)
remainder=>moa_drop(2_di,vec)
if (.not.associated(prefix)) error stop "Take rejected"
if (.not.associated(remainder)) error stop "Drop rejected"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Generate the Fortran modules with the repository Fypp build first. Views alias the original target and require its continued lifetime; use pointer assignment, not allocation. The sketch avoids the nonpositive-drop discrepancy. No generation, compilation or slicing test was run.

local.name: NNLS Fortran 2018
local.description: Nonnegative least-squares solver using BLAS and LAPACK.

classifications.notes: The README gives a solve interface and a randomized test harness with iteration/residual reporting. Multiple solutions may exist; small residuals do not prove recovery of a unique generated vector, and the tests were not run here.

The README gives a solve interface and a randomized test harness with iteration/residual reporting. Multiple solutions may exist; small residuals do not prove recovery of a unique generated vector, and the tests were not run here.

The inspected solve routine forms A-transpose A and A-transpose b, adds variables to a passive set according to the positive projected residual, solves passive normal equations through update_s/DSYSV, and moves toward feasible nonnegative coefficients before updating the residual. This supports constrained L2 least squares D9b1, specifically nonnegative coefficients, not general equality/inequality constraints or a rank-revealing QR method. The code overwrites X from zero and returns ||A X-b||. Material discrepancies: implementation sets MODE=1 and leaves it there on normal completion despite comments/README saying zero; -1 reports iteration exhaustion and returns infinite X/residual. The iteration counter advances only in the inner feasibility loop, so MAXITER is not a strict cap on all outer iterations or linear solves. update_s ignores INFO from both DSYSV workspace query and solve, so rank-deficient/singular normal equations have no safe reported fallback. Normal equations can amplify conditioning issues. No KKT, residual, rank-deficient case or execution was checked.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine, also BIND(C,name="solve"). Fortran callers use module nnls. A(m,n), b(m), x(n), tolerance/residual use C_DOUBLE; dimension/mode/MAXITER scalars use C_INT. The binding lacks VALUE, so C scalar arguments are pointers. There are no INTENT declarations; pass variables rather than relying on input-only dummy semantics. A/b are not assigned in the inspected body; x is overwritten. Actual normal MODE is 1, not the documented 0.

use nnls, only: solve

real(c_double) :: a(3,2), b(3), x(2), res, tol
m=3_c_int
n=2_c_int
maxiter=100_c_int
tol=1.0e-10_c_double
a(:,1)=[1.0_c_double,0.0_c_double,0.0_c_double]
a(:,2)=[0.0_c_double,1.0_c_double,0.0_c_double]
b=[-1.0_c_double,2.0_c_double,1.0_c_double]
call solve(a,b,x,m,n,mode,res,maxiter,tol)
if (mode /= 1_c_int) error stop "NNLS did not finish normally"

local.name: Sherman Morrison update interfaces
local.description: Fortran bindings for matrix-inverse update routines in the TREX Sherman-Morrison project.

classifications.notes: The pinned Fortran interface module exposes update arrays, indices and Slater inverse arguments for Maponi/SM variants through C bindings. This is interface evidence for broad matrix operations, not a verified numerical implementation or ABI audit; backend code is mixed language.

The selected SM1 implementation updates an existing dense inverse after additive column updates A <- A + u*e_j^T, applying the Sherman-Morrison outer-product correction with denominator 1+(A^-1*u)(j). Updates_index is one-based, while C++ matrix storage is row-major. SM1_f is the exported pointer-to-pointer C wrapper. The checked-in Fortran SM1 declaration omits the required by-value BREAKDOWN argument and uses allocatable assumed-shape BIND(C) arrays, whose descriptor ABI is incompatible with these raw pointer-to-pointer parameters. The sketch therefore declares a separate C binding using C_PTR arguments, rather than calling that defective module interface. SM1 only logs a small denominator inside DEBUG1 and still divides by it; BREAKDOWN is not a protective error return. There is no status result or rollback. Review covers the naive update and C wrapper, not Maponi, recursive splitting, Woodbury variants or the independent determinant-scaled IRPF90 kernels.

SOLVERS_BASE dispatches real sparse square linear systems in one-based CSR storage to BCGSTAB or unrestarted GMRES. The BCGSTAB path has no visible denominator/breakdown or early-small-S safeguard. These limitations prevent treating the calling sketch as a checked solver example. classifications.notes: The README describes external-library examples and MUMPS parallel-functionality tests. This is build/use integration rather than a new sparse solver implementation; backend availability and current platform compatibility need separate checks.

classifications.notes: The README describes focused inference tools and a parametric inference engine, explicitly calling the current migration from Python 2 alpha quality. Fortran source remains present, but not every model or API is implemented in Fortran or ported to the current Python generation.

The redistributed DCUHRE driver automatically integrates a vector of user-provided functions over a hyperrectangle. It validates dimension/rule/workspace controls, then DADHRE repeatedly bisects a region with greatest estimated error, evaluates embedded cubature rules and maintains a heap of regions until componentwise absolute/relative criteria or the evaluation budget is reached. The selected default two-dimensional rule has 65 samples per region and the driver supports dimensions 2..15, not a general one-dimensional quadrature entry. IFAIL=0 means the internal estimated-error criterion; IFAIL=1 returns an approximation after budget exhaustion and larger codes report invalid controls. Estimated error is not a rigorous bound. Restart requires preserved compatible workspace and controls; the sketch starts fresh. Review covers driver validation, subdivision/error aggregation and termination paths, not every cubature weight generator or high-dimensional reliability claim.

procedures.summary: External vector-valued globally adaptive hyperrectangular cubature driver.
procedures.usage:
program cubature_sketch
implicit none
external :: dcuhre,integrand
integer :: neval,ifail
double precision :: lower(2),upper(2),value(1),abserr(1),work(5000)
lower=0d0; upper=1d0
call dcuhre(2,1,lower,upper,0,10000,integrand,1d-8,1d-8,0,5000, &
 0,value,abserr,neval,ifail,work)
if(ifail/=0) error stop "inspect cubature diagnostics"
print *,value,abserr,neval
end program
subroutine integrand(ndim,x,numfun,values)
integer :: ndim,numfun
double precision :: x(ndim),values(numfun)
values(1)=x(1)**2+x(2)**2
end subroutine
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Link the complete compatible DCUHRE helper/rule family from this distribution. The workspace and budget are chosen for this two-dimensional one-component sketch only. Independently compare with the analytic integral 2/3; no integral, error estimate or restart was tested.

classifications.notes: NINFOL estimates an observed-information matrix, namely minus the Hessian of a user log-density/log-likelihood at a supplied mode. It evaluates central second differences with successively smaller steps, extrapolates using RID_EX and uses estimated diagonal curvature to scale mixed differences. It does not exponentiate the log function or divide the final log-Hessian by its exponential, despite ambiguous prose in the historical comments. MU must be a genuine stationary maximum with positive diagonal information; otherwise square-root scaling can be invalid. DP must contain nonzero meaningful steps and ITER must be positive. IERR is a real matrix of extrapolation-error estimates, not an integer success flag; ITER=1 sets these estimates to zero without estimating error. MU is temporarily perturbed and restored on normal paths. Review covers diagonal/mixed differencing and extrapolation dispatch, not a general-purpose Hessian routine valid at arbitrary points or a covariance/inference guarantee.

procedures.summary: External mode-specific negative log-Hessian estimation with real-valued error estimates.
procedures.usage:
program information_sketch
implicit none
double precision,external :: log_density
external :: ninfol
double precision :: mode(2),steps(2),information(2,2),errors(2,2),h(4),d2(4),table(4,4)
mode=0d0; steps=0.1d0
call ninfol(log_density,2,mode,0d0,steps,4,information,errors,h,d2,table)
print *,information,errors
! ERRORS is an estimated-error matrix, not a status return.
end program
double precision function log_density(n,x)
integer :: n
double precision :: x(n)
log_density=-0.5d0*(x(1)**2+2d0*x(2)**2)
end function
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The supplied zero mode is stationary with positive diagonal information for this Gaussian log density. Match REAL*8/default INTEGER interfaces and link RID_EX. Compare against diag(1,2) independently; no Hessian, extrapolation or information-matrix result was tested.

The inspected SPLDER routine differences B-spline coefficients recursively to obtain derivative coefficients, then evaluates the lower-degree basis with FPBSPL; the highest derivative has a piecewise-constant branch. This is derivative evaluation of a supplied spline, not numerical differentiation of an arbitrary callback or recovery of derivatives of an unknown sampled function. The caller supplies knots, coefficients and spline degree. The fixed work arrays support the FITPACK degree range through five. The input checks cover derivative order and sorted queries, not complete knot validity or coefficient construction. The nonconstant branch clamps out-of-range queries to endpoints, while the highest-derivative branch differs; keep queries in the documented spline interval. No spline value, derivative or author example was executed.

procedures.summary: External default REAL routine for an existing normalized B-spline representation. Provide t(n), c(n), sorted x(m), y(m), wrk(n), 1 <= k <= 5 and 0 <= nu <= k, with valid knots. Keep query points in [t(k+1),t(n-k)]. Check ier before using y: zero is normal return, ten reports some invalid inputs.
procedures.signature: CALL splder(t, n, c, k, nu, x, y, m, wrk, ier)
procedures.usage:
external :: splder
integer :: ier
real :: t(4), c(4), x(3), y(3), work(4)
t = [0.,0.,1.,1.]
c = [0.,1.,0.,0.]
x = [0.,0.5,1.]
call splder(t,4,c,1,1,x,y,3,work,ier)
if (ier /= 0) error stop "spline derivative failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch of the linear spline s(x)=x on [0,1]. The analytic derivative is one, but no comparison was run. Link fpbspl with splder and use matching default REAL kinds. This sketch supplies coefficients directly and does not demonstrate a fitting routine.

classifications.notes: SPLINT obtains integrals of the normalized B-spline basis from FPINTB and contracts them with the supplied spline coefficients. The helper uses the Gaffney recurrence, reverses sign for reversed integration limits and clips limits to the spline support. E3a3 records quadrature of an already-fitted function, rather than an adaptive integrator for arbitrary functions. The spline is treated as zero outside its base interval according to the public header. The routine has no status or error estimate and assumes valid knots, degree and storage. The helper contains six-element local arrays, consistent with degree at most five; it is not a general arbitrary-degree API. No integral or author example was checked by execution.

procedures.summary: External default REAL function taking t(n), c(n), degree k, scalar limits a,b and wrk(n). Supply a valid normalized B-spline of degree 1..5. wrk returns basis integrals. No ier argument exists. The represented spline is zero outside [t(k+1),t(n-k)] and reversed limits reverse the sign.
procedures.signature: integral = splint(t, n, c, k, a, b, wrk)
procedures.usage:
real, external :: splint
real :: t(4), c(4), work(4), integral
t = [0.,0.,1.,1.]
c = [0.,1.,0.,0.]
integral = splint(t,4,c,1,0.,1.,work)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch integrating the linear spline s(x)=x on [0,1]; its analytic integral is 0.5. Link fpintb with splint, using matching default REAL kinds. No quadrature check or fitting-error estimate was computed. Prefer valid limits within the spline interval when using the documented representation.

local.name: Fortran Probability Distribution Library
local.description: Discrete and continuous distribution functions with C-compatible interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README describes probability/log-probability routines and status outputs. Its identification of c_long_double with 128-bit quad precision is not assumed portable: actual representation is platform/compiler dependent. Overflow/underflow and precision claims have not been independently tested.

poisson_log_pmf evaluates k*LOG(lambda)-lambda-LOG(k!) using the log_factorial helper, and poisson_pmf exponentiates that result and converts it to DP. L5a1p records Poisson probability masses/log masses, not cumulative/inverse probabilities or random draws. K is an INTEGER(C_INT), lambda a REAL(C_DOUBLE); log results use REAL(C_LONG_DOUBLE). C_LONG_DOUBLE is platform-dependent and must not be assumed to be IEEE binary128 despite QP comments. This implementation rejects K<0 and lambda<=0 with error -1, including the valid degenerate lambda=0 distribution, rather than returning its mathematical mass. Check ERR_CODE before interpreting sentinel -1 log values. Log-factorial uses a sum for N<35 and LOG_GAMMA(N+1) otherwise; the integer N+1 can overflow at the representable limit. NaNs and every nonfinite case are not explicitly validated. No probability or overflow test was run.

procedures.summary: Public mod_discrete_dist function, defined in the differently spelled file mod_discrate_dist.f90. K/ERR_CODE use exported IN=C_INT; LAMBDA/result use DP=C_DOUBLE. No BIND(C) is attached to this module procedure; separate C wrappers are outside the review.
procedures.usage:
use mod_math_utils, only: IN,DP,QP
use mod_discrete_dist, only: poisson_pmf,poisson_log_pmf
integer(IN) :: ierr
real(DP) :: mass
real(QP) :: log_mass
mass=poisson_pmf(3_IN,2._DP,ierr)
if(ierr/=0_IN) error stop "Poisson mass failed"
log_mass=poisson_log_pmf(3_IN,2._DP,ierr)
if(ierr/=0_IN) error stop "Poisson log mass failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use finite positive lambda and a moderate nonnegative count. The log API can retain values when a DP probability underflows, but QP is the compiler C_LONG_DOUBLE kind, not a portable precision guarantee. Error -1 is signaled through a separate integer and is not a probability. These module calls do not use the separate C-API wrappers.

procedures.summary: Public log-mass function with the same count/rate checks; returns REAL(QP), not DP. Check ERR_CODE before consuming its sentinel result.

classifications.notes: normal_log_pdf computes -LOG(sigma)-LOG(SQRT(2*pi))-0.5*((x-mu)/sigma)**2 in the configured C_LONG_DOUBLE kind; normal_pdf exponentiates and converts to C_DOUBLE. L5a1n records univariate normal densities/log densities, not a CDF, tail probability, inverse or random generator. SIGMA is a positive standard deviation, not variance; nonpositive values return ERR_CODE=-1. The source does not explicitly reject NaNs/nonfinite X/MU/SIGMA. QP is a C_LONG_DOUBLE alias with platform-dependent precision. A log-density sentinel of -1 on failure is not distinguishable from a valid value without checking ERR_CODE. Density conversion can underflow or overflow independently of the log representation. No density values or tail behavior were run.

procedures.summary: Public REAL(DP) normal density function with REAL(DP) X/MU/SIGMA and INTEGER(IN) output ERR_CODE. DP=C_DOUBLE; the log counterpart returns QP=C_LONG_DOUBLE.
procedures.usage:
use mod_math_utils, only: IN,DP,QP
use mod_continuous_dist, only: normal_pdf,normal_log_pdf
integer(IN) :: ierr
real(DP) :: density
real(QP) :: log_density
density=normal_pdf(0._DP,0._DP,1._DP,ierr)
if(ierr/=0_IN) error stop "Normal density failed"
log_density=normal_log_pdf(0._DP,0._DP,1._DP,ierr)
if(ierr/=0_IN) error stop "Normal log density failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Supply finite inputs with positive standard deviation. A density is not a probability and may exceed one for narrow distributions. Do not mistake the log API for an error estimate or the QP name for fixed quadruple precision.

procedures.summary: Public REAL(QP) log-density function; positive-sigma check and separate error code are part of the contract.

local.name: M_datapac
local.description: Module adaptation of NIST DATAPAC statistical and probability procedures.

classifications.notes: The README identifies original James Filliben routines, a module adaptation and documentation independent of Dataplot. The original package stopped development; no blanket accuracy or current-compiler verification is inferred for all inherited routines.

The selected real64 module mean routine directly sums X(1:N) and divides by N, with special diagnostics for one/all-equal observations. median copies/sorts the selected observations into fixed COMMON workspace and returns the middle element or the average of the two middle elements. The median count limit is 15000. Both require N<=SIZE(X); invalid counts print diagnostics and return without a defined output/status rather than throwing a structured error. The sketch imports M_datapac__d directly to select the real64 implementation. This is descriptive sample location, not distribution fitting or a new numerical verification of all DATAPAC routines.

procedures.summary: REAL64 module sample mean over the first N entries. Iwrite=0 suppresses the normal result report, but input/special-case diagnostics can still print.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use M_datapac__d, only: mean, median
real(real64) :: x(4), average, middle
x=[1.0_real64,2.0_real64,4.0_real64,5.0_real64]
call mean(x,size(x),0,average)
call median(x,size(x),0,middle)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use 1<=N<=SIZE(X), and N<=15000 for median. Diagnostics do not supply a success flag; invalid counts leave result undefined. Median uses shared COMMON workspace and is not a reentrant routine.

procedures.summary: REAL64 module median with fixed 15000-value shared workspace and sorting dependency.

classifications.notes: The real64 var routine uses two passes: sum to form the arithmetic mean, then sum squared centered differences and divide by N-1. It returns zero with diagnostics for N=1 or constant data. N<1 prints an error and returns with Xvar undefined; N>SIZE(X) is not checked. This supports descriptive sample variance, not a robust, compensated or streaming estimator, and the singleton result is a repository convention rather than an unbiased sample-variance estimate. No numerical result was computed.

procedures.summary: REAL64 two-pass sample variance using denominator N-1 for nonconstant N>1 data.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use M_datapac__d, only: var
real(real64) :: x(4), variance
x=[1.0_real64,2.0_real64,4.0_real64,5.0_real64]
call var(x,size(x),0,variance)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Supply at least two finite observations for the usual sample-variance interpretation. Invalid counts lack a returned status; Iwrite=0 does not suppress diagnostics. No residual/accuracy comparison was performed.

local.name: HARMONIE Monitor
local.description: Station-based forecast verification statistics and contingency-table scores.

classifications.notes: The documentation overview describes scores, matched model/observation samples and web presentation. It says station-based verification is less suitable for moving platforms or fields; it evaluates predictions rather than generating a weather forecast.

CALC_CORR computes descriptive statistics for paired observations: both means/sample standard deviations, signed bias Ymean-Xmean, RMSE, centered population-scale difference spread and Pearson correlation. This supports elementary analysis of paired data; it does not compute a significance test, confidence interval or distribution model. The native routine uses default-real one-pass sums, so cancellation can affect nearly constant/large-offset data. Require NOBS>1 and finite prefiltered pairs because no missing-value or small-sample checks are performed. Constant-series correlation remains the initialized zero rather than returning a distinct undefined-correlation status. ABS under square roots masks negative roundoff terms, and the standard-deviation and centered-error denominators are not the same. Review covers the complete short calculation, not forecast-verification inference or numerical stability by execution.

procedures.summary: External paired descriptive statistics with default-real arrays and no status output.
procedures.usage:
real :: x(3),y(3),xm,ym,sx,sy,bias,rmse,spread,corr
x=[1.,2.,3.]; y=[1.2,1.8,3.1]
call calc_corr(3,x,y,xm,ym,sx,sy,bias,rmse,spread,corr)
print *,bias,rmse,corr
! Require more than one finite pair; handle constant-series correlation explicitly.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Default REAL contract; preserve the documented bias direction and denominator conventions. A returned zero correlation is not necessarily evidence of no association. No statistic, cancellation or missing-data path was tested.

classifications.notes: INI_CONT configures thresholds and ACC_CONT tallies observation/forecast category pairs for each experiment. The native loops use strict greater-than threshold comparisons, with categories numbered zero through NCLASS, so an observation equal to a threshold remains in the lower category. The input scatter layout stores observations in row one and forecast-minus-observation differences in later rows; ACC_CONT adds the observation back before classifying each forecast. It resets the count table on each call rather than accumulating successive batches. Supply initialized pointer-backed SCATTER_TYPE arrays, increasing thresholds, valid parameter indices and compatible experiment/table dimensions. The shared module state is not independent per caller. This is contingency-table construction L2b, not a score calculation, categorical hypothesis test or probability estimate.

procedures.summary: Public threshold-category contingency tally for initialized Monitor scatter records.
procedures.usage:
use types, only: scatter_type
use contingency, only: ini_cont,acc_cont,cont_table
type(scatter_type) :: dat(1)
call ini_cont(1,2,1,[2],1,[1],reshape([0.,1.],[2,1]))
dat(1)%n=3; allocate(dat(1)%dat(2,3))
dat(1)%dat(1,:)=[-0.5,0.5,1.5] ! Observations.
dat(1)%dat(2,:)=[0.1,-0.1,0.2] ! Forecast minus observation.
call acc_cont(1,1,dat)
print *,cont_table(1)%table
! Each ACC_CONT call starts a fresh table.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use matching Monitor TYPES/CONTINGENCY modules and valid pointer lifetimes; follow package cleanup when done. Threshold equality, forecast reconstruction and per-call reset are part of the contract. No counts, table dimensions or forecast scores were run.

local.name: M_random
local.description: Fortran pseudorandom generators, seed helpers and sampling utilities.

classifications.notes: The README lists intrinsic-seed supplements, generator state interfaces, shuffling and random scalar/string utilities. Generator quality, independence of streams and platform reproducibility need later review; none is presented as cryptographically validated.

The public Mersenne-Twister real adapters turn a masked 32-bit pseudorandom word stored in INT64 into a REAL(SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307)) uniform variate. REAL2 scales by 2^-32 for [0,1), while REAL3 adds one half before scaling for (0,1). MT state is explicit and advances on each draw. The core twist/temper recurrence was inspected, but the name RAND64 refers to storage kind, not 64 independent random bits. Initialize state explicitly with an INT32 seed. This is pseudorandom sampling, not a cryptographic generator, a statistical test result or a guarantee of independent streams.

procedures.summary: Public half-open uniform adapter taking mutable explicit generator state.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: int32,real64
use M_random, only: mtprng_state,mtprng_init,mtprng_rand_real2
type(mtprng_state) :: state
real(real64) :: u
call mtprng_init(12345_int32,state)
u=mtprng_rand_real2(state)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. REAL64 matches the selected IEEE64 kind on conventional supported builds; confirm that kind on a new platform. Use the REAL3 adapter when both endpoints must be excluded. No sequence, interval histogram or stream independence test was run.

classifications.notes: SCRAMBLE allocates integers 1 through N and permutes them by two full sweeps of random swaps, choosing each partner over the entire array using intrinsic RANDOM_NUMBER. The result preserves a permutation structurally, but this is not a Fisher-Yates shuffle and does not generally give every permutation equal probability. L6a16 records the permutations subset, not Poisson/Pareto/Pascal generation. Its RNG is the Fortran intrinsic state, separate from explicit Mersenne-Twister state. Use nonnegative N and validate allocation/large-size behavior independently. The mapping records the implemented permutation generator with an explicit distribution limitation.

procedures.summary: Public function returning an allocatable default-integer permutation; no RNG-state argument.
procedures.usage:
use M_random, only: scramble
integer,allocatable :: order(:)
! Seed the intrinsic generator separately when reproducibility is required.
order=scramble(10)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Do not use this two-sweep shuffle as evidence of uniform random permutations. MTPRNG_INIT does not seed the intrinsic RANDOM_NUMBER stream used here. No permutation-frequency or empty-input test was run.

classifications.notes: MTPRNG_INIT initializes the explicit 624-word MT state from an INT32 seed using a masked Knuth-style recurrence and sets the position to request a twist on the next draw. It does not seed the Fortran intrinsic generator or the separate KISS generator. The API can keep several state objects, but distinct seeds alone do not certify disjoint or independent streams. This mapping is a seeding/state service, without a new period, portability or statistical-quality verification.

procedures.summary: Public state initializer with INT32 seed and output MTPRNG_STATE.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: int32
use M_random, only: mtprng_state,mtprng_init
type(mtprng_state) :: state
call mtprng_init(12345_int32,state)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Preserve the complete state if resuming a sequence. An explicitly chosen seed aids reproducibility but does not establish cross-build bit identity or independent parallel streams. No seed or restart experiment was run.

local.name: npregfast
local.description: Nonparametric regression with factor-by-curve interactions, local polynomials and splines.

classifications.notes: The README documents derivatives, binning, bootstrap intervals and an allometric option; the repository contains a Fortran computation source. Statistical coverage and performance depend on smoother choices and are not independently verified.

The selected Reg1D kernel computes local polynomial regression at one query using bandwidth H relative to RANGO and observation weights W. Kernel 1 is compact Epanechnikov, 2 triangular and 3 Gaussian; IFCV=1 removes observations at exactly the query value. It centers polynomial powers at X0, calls the local weighted regression helper and returns fitted level, first/second polynomial coefficients, standard errors, R-squared and helper status in PRED(1:8). The third polynomial coefficient is not multiplied by 2, so PRED(3) is not automatically the second derivative. At least seven positive-weight local observations are required even for lower degree. The fixed four-column local design and output accesses motivate restricting this sketch to degree 2. Invalid/insufficient fits set all PRED=-1, so failure cannot be detected from PRED(1) alone. This is a selected smoothing kernel, not the complete factor-by-curve/bootstrap R workflow.

procedures.summary: External double-precision one-query local polynomial smoother returning a packed eight-value result.
procedures.usage:
external :: Reg1D
integer :: i
double precision :: x(9),y(9),w(9),pred(8)
do i=1,9
 x(i)=dble(i-1)/8d0
end do
y=1d0+x+x*x; w=1d0
call Reg1D(x,y,w,9,1d0,2,0.5d0,pred,1d0,3,0)
if(pred(8)/=0d0) error stop "local fit rejected"
! PRED(3) is a quadratic coefficient; second derivative would be 2*PRED(3).
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use finite data, positive bandwidth/range and more than six retained local observations. Link the package weighted-regression helpers; the large source file also contains other package routines. The sketch fixes degree 2 and does not validate derivative uncertainty or bootstrap inference. No fit, failure status or derivative result was tested.

classifications.notes: The bundled public LSQ module implements sequential weighted least-squares reduction using STARTUP, INCLUD and REGCF (AS75/AS274 lineage). With unit weights it estimates ordinary multiple-linear regression coefficients from raw rows, including a caller-supplied leading constant when fit_const is true. STARTUP allocates shared saved state; INCLUD overwrites XROW and deliberately omits dimension checks. REGCF back-substitutes the reduction, calling TOLSET if needed, and uses negative IFAULT values for detected deficient diagonals rather than proving numerical rank. The module is stateful and not a reentrant independent-fit object. Review covers initialization, row inclusion and coefficient recovery; variable-selection/inference routines in the same file are not promoted by this claim.

procedures.summary: Public LSQ module initialization followed by destructive row inclusion and coefficient recovery.
procedures.signature:
CALL startup(NVAR,FIT_CONST)
CALL includ(WEIGHT,XROW,YELEM)
CALL regcf(BETA,NREQ,IFAULT)
procedures.usage:
use lsq, only: startup,includ,regcf
integer :: i,ifault
double precision :: row(3),beta(3),x1(4),x2(4),y(4)
x1=[0d0,1d0,0d0,1d0]; x2=[0d0,0d0,1d0,1d0]
y=1d0+2d0*x1+3d0*x2
call startup(2,.true.)
do i=1,4
 row=[1d0,x1(i),x2(i)]
 call includ(1d0,row,y(i))
end do

local.name: quantregpy
local.description: Experimental Python quantile-regression interface adapted from R quantreg Fortran routines.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly suspends development as of September 2021 and labels the implementation experimental. It documents modified f2py Fortran and translated R code; completeness relative to R quantreg and current Python compatibility are not established.

RQFNB solves the bounded linear-program form used for multiple quantile regression with a Frisch-Newton primal-dual interior-point iteration and weighted normal-equation solves. The selected TAU=0.5 case is multiple median/L1 regression and supports L8c3; other quantiles use asymmetric check loss rather than an ordinary Lp norm. The caller supplies A=X-transpose, cost=-response, RHS=(1-tau)*sum(X,rows), unit upper bounds and initial WN(:,1)=1-tau, as the Python wrapper establishes. Regression coefficients are minus WP(:,1), not the raw primal/dual vector in WN. Iterations are hard-capped at fifty; INFO primarily reports normal-equation factorization and may remain zero on iteration exhaustion, so NIT and independent optimality/residual checks are needed. Inputs/workspaces are overwritten and boundary quantiles or singular designs are not supported by this sketch. Review covers initialization, predictor/corrector loop, solve dispatch and wrapper sign conventions, not censored/constrained variants or statistical inference.

procedures.summary: External dense Frisch-Newton quantile-regression LP kernel, selected here for median regression.

external :: rqfnb
integer,parameter :: n=6,p=2
integer :: nit(3),info
double precision :: x(n,p),response(n),a(p,n),cost(n),rhs(p),d(n),u(n),wn(n,9),wp(p,p+3),coef(p)
x(:,1)=1d0; x(:,2)=[0d0,1d0,2d0,3d0,4d0,5d0]
response=[1d0,3d0,5d0,7d0,9d0,20d0]
a=transpose(x); cost=-response; rhs=0.5d0*sum(x,dim=1)
d=1d0; u=1d0; wn=0d0; wn(:,1)=0.5d0; wp=0d0
call rqfnb(n,p,a,cost,rhs,d,u,0.99995d0,1d-6,wn,wp,nit,info)
if(info/=0.or.nit(1)>=50) error stop "inspect LP factorization/iteration diagnostics"
coef=-wp(:,1)
print *,coef
! Check median-regression optimality independently; INFO alone is insufficient.

local.name: rpact AS 251
local.description: R/Rcpp integration of Fortran multivariate-normal probability integrals with product correlations.

classifications.notes: The README identifies AS 251 and explicitly discusses single-precision REAL/C++ float conversions. This is a specialized correlation structure and arithmetic interface, not an arbitrary covariance-matrix probability evaluator.

MVNPRD computes a standardized multivariate-normal rectangular probability for off-diagonal correlations rho(i,j)=BPD(i)*BPD(j), using independent-coordinate factors and one-dimensional adaptive Simpson integration of products of conditional normal probabilities. L5b1n records normal multivariate probabilities, restricted to this product-correlation family rather than arbitrary covariance matrices. N is limited to 1..50 and ABS(BPD)<1. A contains upper and B lower limits; INF=0/1/2 select lower-to-infinity, minus-infinity-to-upper and finite intervals. IERC selects derivative-based or interval-halving error control, and HINC<=0 is replaced by 0.24. IFAULT distinguishes input, integration/evaluation-limit and requested-bound failures; do not treat the header accuracy claim as a verified rigorous bound. The defining Fortran uses default REAL and the C++ wrapper converts to float, so R double inputs do not give a double-precision integration kernel. The Student-t path is excluded. No probability or error-bound test was run.

local.name: SparseReg MATLAB toolbox
local.description: Sparse-regression MATLAB toolbox with compiled Fortran estimation components.

classifications.notes: The README gives sparse-regression scope, and the source tree includes private Fortran GLM/least-squares/penalty routines. Individual penalty families, optimization guarantees and MATLAB interoperability need more detailed procedure-level review.

PENALIZED_L2_REGRESSION in the public Fortran SPARSEREG module performs cyclic coordinate updates for weighted multiple-linear regression with selected separable penalties. The reviewed ENET branch uses rho*((eta-1)*beta**2/2+(2-eta)*abs(beta)), with eta in [1,2], a different parameter convention from GLMnet PARM. SUM_X_SQUARES must be precomputed as sum(WT*X(:,i)**2); unpenalized columns use a direct coordinate minimizer and all required coordinate curvatures must be positive. ESTIMATE is updated in place and MAXITERS can be reset from a nonpositive value, but no actual iteration count or success code is returned. Shape mismatch, objective increase, convergence and exhaustion can all end without distinct diagnostics. Some invalid threshold inputs leave the function result unassigned, so validate sizes, weights and tuning values first. Although the file is under MATLAB private/, its module procedures are public by default and do not require a MEX entry for this direct call. Review covers the native weighted ENET path, not every nonconvex penalty, GLM family or MATLAB wrapper.

logical :: penalized(p)
x(:,1)=1._DBLE_PREC; x(:,2)=[0._DBLE_PREC,1._DBLE_PREC,2._DBLE_PREC, &
 3._DBLE_PREC,4._DBLE_PREC,5._DBLE_PREC]

end do
penalized=[.false.,.true.]; maxiters=1000
call PENALIZED_L2_REGRESSION(beta,x,y,weights,0.1_DBLE_PREC,curvature, &
 penalized,maxiters,"ENET",[1.5_DBLE_PREC])
print *,beta

The external BS02R routine sums centered third and fourth powers, then normalizes them with the N-1 sample variance: SKEW=sum(delta**3)/(N*SDEV**3) and CURT=sum(delta**4)/(N*VAR**2)-3. These are the exact implemented sample-shape conventions, not claimed unbiased skewness/kurtosis estimators. Require N>=2 with N available finite values. The input-length check is commented out; for constant data the code leaves SKEW=CURT=0 rather than flagging undefined normalized moments. No hypothesis test, robustness or numerical accuracy was verified. Unlike the BS01R examples with internal routines, this reviewed file supplies a standalone external procedure.

procedures.summary: Default-REAL sample skewness and excess-kurtosis subroutine using sample-variance normalization and no status output.

real :: x(4), skew, excess
external :: bs02r
x=[1.0,2.0,3.0,5.0]
call bs02r(x,size(x),skew,excess)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use N>=2 and nonconstant finite data. Results follow the recorded N versus N-1 normalization and are not bias-corrected estimators. Constant data produces zero sentinels without a diagnostic. No compile or numerical check was made.

simpson_integrator_vals integrates a vector of samples over a presumed uniformly spaced finite grid. Odd sample counts use composite Simpson 1/3; even counts use 1/3 up to the last four samples and a final 3/8 panel. H2a1b2 records nonautomatic quadrature from sampled data; no callback, adaptive error control or nonuniform-coordinate support is implied. At least three samples are needed for odd N and four for even N; the code does not validate these sizes, and N=1 divides by zero while small even counts address invalid elements. The routine returns only a scalar estimate and no error/status. Other integration, optimization and algebra routines remain outside this source review. No polynomial reference integral or upstream test was run.

procedures.summary: Public double-precision function in numa__integrate, re-exported by numa. Input yi is an assumed-shape vector of equally spaced function values including both endpoints; xmin/xmax are the corresponding interval endpoints. The number of samples selects the 1/3-only or mixed 1/3+3/8 rule.
procedures.usage:
use numa__integrate, only: simpson_integrator_vals
double precision :: y(5), area
! Samples of x**2 at x=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.
y = [0.0d0, 0.0625d0, 0.25d0, 0.5625d0, 1.0d0]
area = simpson_integrator_vals(y, 0.0d0, 1.0d0)
! Analytic reference is 1/3; no comparison was executed here.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile the library with its preprocessing/include settings. Enforce a uniform grid and valid sample count yourself: no coordinate array, tolerance or status is supplied. Reversed endpoints change the sign algebraically; singular/discontinuous data and accuracy are not certified. Other integrator names in the same module do not inherit this review.

numFort::fft is an in-place recursive radix-two complex transform: split odd/even-indexed subsequences, recurse and recombine with exp(-2*pi*i*k/N). It computes an unnormalized forward transform. Correct radix-two use requires a positive power-of-two length; the code does not enforce that precondition, and odd lengths leave unmatched entries. No inverse, normalization parameter, multidimensional transform or general mixed-radix support is claimed. The enclosing module imports QUADPACK, LAPACK95 and minFun, so this routine is not a standalone build merely because its arithmetic uses intrinsics. No transform accuracy or timing was tested.

procedures.summary: Recursive module subroutine overwriting a COMPLEX(DP) vector with the forward unnormalized transform; use power-of-two sizes.

use kinds, only: DP
use numFort, only: fft
complex(DP) :: x(4)
x=cmplx([1.0_DP,0.0_DP,0.0_DP,0.0_DP],0.0_DP,DP)
call fft(x)

classifications.notes: The sampled-data trapZZ overload, exposed through generic trapZ, applies the trapezoidal sum using ONE width abs(x(1)-x(2)) for every panel. It is therefore restricted to an equally spaced ascending grid in this mapping, with at least two x values and matching y length. Nonuniform-grid integration is not implemented by this overload. Descending grids do not produce signed reversal because the width is absolute; mismatched lengths and short arrays are unchecked. There is no error estimate or adaptive refinement. The scalar and vector rk4_explicit_step overloads evaluate the classical four Runge-Kutta stages at t, t+h/2, t+h/2 and t+h, then form the 1:2:2:1 weighted update. I1a1a records an explicit one-step ODE initial-value method. The parent module declares public generics and implementations live in a submodule; compile/link both rather than assuming the interface module supplies code. H is declared INOUT but is unchanged in these implementations, and T is input-only. Caller chooses H and advances time; there is no local error estimate, rejection loop, stiffness detection or returned status. Scalar and vector callbacks use rkp=ISO_FORTRAN_ENV real64 and have distinct explicit interfaces. No ODE, convergence-order or stiffness experiment was run.

procedures.summary: Public generic in rungekutta_explicit, implemented by scalar/vector module subroutines in submodule rk4_explicit. F(t,y0) returns either a scalar or SIZE(y0) vector. Y0 is input, Y output and H an INOUT variable; use distinct input/output state storage.
procedures.signature: CALL rk4_explicit_step(f, t, y0, y, h)
procedures.usage:
use kindSettings, only: rkp
use rungekutta_explicit, only: rk4_explicit_step
real(rkp) :: t,y0,y,h
! Supply a matching real(rkp) scalar RHS(t,y0) callback.
t=0._rkp; y0=1._rkp; h=0.01_rkp
call rk4_explicit_step(rhs,t,y0,y,h)
t=t+h; y0=y
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Callback fragment. Build kindSettings, functionInterface and the parent module before its RK4 submodule. H must be a variable because its dummy is INOUT, although this method does not adapt it. Do not alias Y0 and Y. Accuracy and stability depend on problem and caller-selected step size.

The external CG routine forms the initial residual, then applies conjugate-gradient alpha/beta recurrences with dense MATMUL and dot products, updating X until the infinity norm of the recursively updated residual is small. D2b1b records real symmetric positive-definite dense systems, not arbitrary matrices or a sparse storage API. It has no iteration cap, SPD/breakdown checks or status return; an exact initial solution still enters the loop with ERR=1 and can divide 0/0. EPS>=1 can skip all work. Recompute the true residual independently and avoid treating the recurrence as an error certificate. The same source file contains a separate fixed 2-by-2 demonstration MAIN; extract the external CG procedure before linking to another main program. No system was solved for this catalog.

procedures.summary: External default-REAL dense solver with explicit-shape A(N,N), X(N), B(N) and scalar EPSILON. X is the initial guess on entry and is overwritten. There are no INTENT declarations or returned status; the source file also defines cg_code MAIN.
procedures.signature: CALL CG(n, a, x, b, epsilon)
procedures.usage:
! Extract the external CG routine from its demonstration file before linking.
external :: cg
real :: a(2,2),b(2),x(2)
a=reshape([4.,1.,1.,3.],[2,2]); b=[1.,2.]; x=0.
call cg(2,a,x,b,1.e-6)
! Independently check maxval(abs(matmul(a,x)-b)).
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Default-REAL SPD example fragment, not a robust general linear-system driver. A nonzero initial residual, positive tolerance below 1, positive curvature and an external execution limit are necessary for this unguarded implementation. Separate MAIN from the callable external routine; compiling the file unchanged alongside another PROGRAM causes a duplicate-main conflict.

classifications.notes: The bisec_code program halves a sign-changing interval for its hardcoded real-coefficient cubic x**3-x-2 and prints one selected real root. F1a1 records that polynomial root demonstration, not a general all-roots algorithm or root isolation. The linked external function F supplies the fixed cubic; a and b are assigned in MAIN rather than user inputs. There is no initial-bracket validation for a modified problem, iteration limit, stagnation guard or returned status. Termination uses an absolute function residual of 1e-6 in default REAL, not a bound on root-location error. No program output was executed.

newton_raphson calls supplied residual/Jacobian functions, solves J(x)*dx=-F(x) using the companion unpivoted LU path, adds the step and stops on the sum of absolute coordinate changes. fixPoint repeatedly assigns G(x) and uses the same step-change test. F2 records real nonlinear systems/fixed-point iteration, not guaranteed global convergence or a singular-Jacobian-safe Newton solver. Callbacks return allocatable default-REAL vectors/matrices. ITE is both maximum iterations and successful iteration count; ITE<=0 leaves OK unassigned. EPS must be positive and meaningful for default REAL. There is no residual, contractivity, pivot or finite-value validation. The companion LU does not pivot or report breakdown, and the whole module depends on it even when only fixPoint is used. No nonlinear solve or convergence test was executed.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine with mutable X(:), INOUT integer ITE, input default-REAL EPS and output logical OK. F returns allocatable REAL(:); J returns allocatable REAL(:,:). OK tests step size, not residual size.
procedures.signature: CALL newton_raphson(F, J, x, ite, eps, ok)
procedures.usage:
use module_no_linear_equations, only: newton_raphson
real :: x(2)=[1.,1.]
integer :: iterations
logical :: ok
! Supply explicit-interface F and J returning allocatable default-REAL arrays.
iterations=50
call newton_raphson(f,j,x,iterations,1.e-5,ok)
if(.not.ok) error stop "Newton step test not satisfied"
! Independently evaluate F(x) and check its norm.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Problem-callback fragment. Use a positive iteration cap, conformable allocatable callback results and a Jacobian suitable for the unpivoted LU routine. Small steps alone do not establish a root. Preserve an external iteration limit and check finite values/residuals; the upstream example tolerance 1e-10 should not be mistaken for guaranteed default-REAL accuracy.

Interpolation::lagrange directly evaluates the global Lagrange interpolation polynomial by multiplying all nodal factors for each datum and summing the weighted ordinates. lagrangep applies that scalar function to query points, allocating yEval only if not already allocated. Require nonempty equal-length data with distinct abscissae; no duplicate-node, conditioning or overflow check exists. An already allocated yEval must match the query length because the routine does not resize it. This is global polynomial interpolation, not piecewise splines: the naturalcubicspline routines are unimplemented ERROR STOP placeholders, and are not mapped. No interpolation check was run.

procedures.summary: REAL(DP) scalar module interpolation function using direct product-form global Lagrange polynomials.
procedures.usage:
use Constants, only: DP
use Interpolation, only: lagrange
real(DP) :: nodes(3), values(3), y
nodes=[0.0_DP,1.0_DP,2.0_DP]
values=[0.0_DP,1.0_DP,4.0_DP]
y=lagrange(nodes,values,0.5_DP)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use distinct nodes and equal, nonempty arrays. The direct product formula is not a barycentric stability guarantee. The reviewed binding converts a C function pointer to a module callback adapter and forwards arrays/controls to the bundled modern QUADPACK implementation. Integrands return C_DOUBLE and accept x by value plus an args-array pointer. Workspaces, callback/args lifetimes, compatible C_INT/default-integer and C_DOUBLE/native-real ABI and valid tolerances remain caller responsibilities. The implementation saves/restores callback slots around the call; OpenMP threadprivate directives only provide separate thread state when compiled with OpenMP. This is a source review of the binding/dispatch, not a new audit or numerical validation of QUADPACK or a guarantee of nested backend reentrancy. DQAGS_WRAPPER exposes finite-interval adaptive quadrature with error estimation/extrapolation. RESULT is the integral approximation; ABSERR is an estimated absolute error, NEVAL counts evaluations, IER is the solver status and LAST describes the used partition. IWORK has LIMIT entries and WORK has 4*LIMIT entries. Endpoint/interior difficulty and invalid inputs can return nonzero IER; a small estimated error is not a rigorous bound.

procedures.summary: Public C-interoperable finite-interval QUADPACK binding with explicit work and partition outputs.
procedures.usage:
use iso_c_binding
use quadpack_wrappers, only: dqags_wrapper
integer(c_int),parameter :: limit=100
integer(c_int) :: iwork(limit),neval,ier,last
real(c_double) :: work(4*limit),args(1),result,abserr
type(c_funptr) :: fptr
! FPTR is a valid C_FUNLOC callback: real(c_double) function f(x,args) bind(c),
! with X passed VALUE and ARGS(*) passed by reference. Initialize it first.
args=0._c_double
call dqags_wrapper(fptr,0._c_double,1._c_double,1.e-8_c_double, &
 1.e-8_c_double,result,abserr,neval,ier,limit,iwork,work,args,1_c_int,last)
if(ier/=0) error stop "inspect QUADPACK diagnostics"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-callback-setup fragment. Match pointer lifetimes/ABI and inspect status, integrand behavior and estimated error independently. No finite integral, callback execution, thread or nesting behavior was tested.

classifications.notes: HYBRD_WRAPPER exposes a MINPACK local nonlinear-system solve without user Jacobian entries, using a finite-difference Powell-hybrid driver and an explicitly supplied C callback address. It constructs the simplified driver workspace/scaling/control defaults while allowing MAXFEV to be passed through, then maps backend INFO=5 to 4. The callback fills N residuals from N parameters; dimensions are not passed in that callback ABI and must be known by its implementation. INFO=1 is a step-tolerance termination, not independent proof that all residuals are small; other codes need MINPACK interpretation. The module stores callback/args pointers, uses optional OpenMP threadprivate state and does not save/restore that state in this particular root wrapper, unlike the reviewed quadrature bindings. Nested calls on the same thread can overwrite context, and parallel calls without the appropriate OpenMP build share it. Review covers the wrapper and adapter, not every native MINPACK algorithm path or a global root guarantee.

mod_numerical::linint uses locate to choose adjacent samples and forms their affine weighted combination. E1a records univariate piecewise-linear interpolation, not global high-degree polynomial fitting. The interval index is clamped so out-of-range queries linearly extrapolate using the first/last pair. local.name: Robust Gauss Newton
local.description: Fortran nonlinear least-squares optimization with sampling and null-space heuristics.

classifications.notes: The README identifies three heuristics, a Rosenbrock example and HYMOD calibration. Robustness and comparative performance are research claims, not independent results here; the example physical model is not universally validated.

The public RGN module routine minimizes one-half the sum of squared user residuals subject to simple lower/upper parameter bounds. It estimates the Jacobian by bound-clipped finite differences, forms J-transpose*r and J-transpose*J, adjusts the active bounds and solves a reduced Gauss-Newton system with step/globalization logic. This is constrained nonlinear least squares; Robust in the project name does not establish an outlier-resistant loss function. Callers must supply consistent residuals and scalar objective, finite strictly separated bounds and the module-defined kinds. ERROR reports callback/interface failures, while INFO%TERMFLAG distinguishes iteration limit, small objective change, no reduction and small parameter change; ERROR=0 alone does not certify convergence. Some input/storage errors use STOP or console interaction rather than a clean status return. Review covers the native bounded iteration and concrete Rosenbrock callback convention, not convergence guarantees, rank-deficient behavior or a global optimum claim.

procedures.summary: Public module bounded nonlinear least-squares driver with a residual/objective callback.
procedures.usage:
program bounded_ls_sketch
use constantsMod, only: ik,rk
use rgnMod, only: rgn,rgnConvType,rgnInfoType,setDefaultRgnConvergeSettings
implicit none
type(rgnConvType) :: cnv
type(rgnInfoType) :: info
real(rk) :: x0(2),lo(2),hi(2),x(2)
integer(ik) :: error
character(100) :: message
x0=[-1._rk,0._rk]; lo=[-1.5_rk,-1._rk]; hi=[1.5_rk,3._rk]
call setDefaultRgnConvergeSettings(cnv)
cnv%iterMax=200_ik; cnv%dumpResults=0_ik
error=0_ik; message=""
call rgn(residual,2_ik,2_ik,x0,lo,hi,cnv,x,info,error,message)
if(error/=0_ik) error stop "RGN callback/interface failure"
print *,info%termFlag,info%f,x
contains
subroutine residual(nPar,nSim,x,r,f,timeFunc,error,message)
 integer(ik),intent(in) :: nPar,nSim
 real(rk),intent(in) :: x(:)
 real(rk),intent(out) :: r(:),f,timeFunc
 integer(ik),intent(inout) :: error
 character(100),intent(inout) :: message
 r(1)=1._rk-x(1); r(2)=10._rk*(x(2)-x(1)**2)
 f=0.5_rk*sum(r*r); timeFunc=0._rk; error=0_ik; message=""
end subroutine
end program

local.name: rrelaxiv
local.description: R interface to the Fortran RELAX-IV minimum-cost network-flow solver.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes a simplified sanitized interface from an advanced raw interface and identifies research-use restrictions. Solver assumptions, integer limits and numerical results need later review; graph optimization is not classified as a geometric mesh solver.

RELAXALG builds network incidence lists and invokes the RELAX4 relaxation/auction algorithm for integer capacitated minimum-cost flow. The wrapper takes positive supplies in B1 and converts them to internal demands with B=-B1, despite a lower-level R comment calling them demands. It overwrites capacities with residual capacities, supplies with final internal deficits, flows X1 and reduced costs RC1. CRASH=1 selects auction initialization. Valid node indices, nonnegative capacities, balanced supplies and bounded integer arithmetic are caller responsibilities. The wrapper starts FEASIBLE=1 but some large-cost/capacity rejection paths return before copying that flag or output arrays, so FEASIBLE1 alone is not a universal validation status. COMMON blocks preclude concurrent independent calls. Review covers wrapper/list construction and selected price-flow/feasibility paths, not complexity bounds, sensitivity analysis or every augmentation case.

call RELAXALG(n,na,startn,endn,cost,capacity,supply,flow,rc,crash,large,feasible)
if(feasible/=1) error stop "flow not reported feasible"

local.name: ScipyDIRECT
local.description: Python interface to Gablonsky Fortran DIRECT bound-constrained global search.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the Fortran implementation and explicitly says SciPy now supersedes this package. Historical interface availability is preserved; current Python compatibility and finite-run global optimality are not established.

DIRECT normalizes finite box bounds, samples rectangle centers, chooses potentially optimal rectangles and divides their longest sides into thirds. ALGMETHOD selects the original or modified selection strategy. The inspected serial evaluation path rescales coordinates before invoking FCN(N,X,F,FLAG,IIDATA,IISIZE,DDATA,IDSIZE,CDATA,ICSIZE); FLAG=0 marks a defined objective and positive values mark hidden infeasibility. No derivative or explicit Lipschitz constant is required. Global search is an algorithmic scope, not a finite-budget certificate of the global optimum. Positive IERROR values include evaluation/iteration budget and rectangle size terminations. Fixed capacities include MaxDim=64 and Maxfunc=90000; MAXF is not necessarily a strict evaluation ceiling, especially while searching for a feasible point. The COMMON control state and fixed work storage require care for simultaneous calls. This review covers driver, selection and serial callback dispatch, not every rectangle bookkeeping routine.

classifications.notes: The brief README supports random generation and C++ interoperability. Individual generator families, seeding, stream properties and statistical quality need source-level review; no specific generator is inferred from the older discovery description.

rng_m provides object-owned MT19937 state with 624 INT32 words, single-seed expansion, a twist recurrence and bitwise tempering. The selected uint32 binding masks signed INT32 output into a nonnegative INT64 result, carrying a 32-bit integer payload rather than generating 64 random bits or a real-valued variate. L6a21 records intended discrete uniform pseudorandom output. An unseeded state falls back to seed 5489; explicitly seeding is shown. Seed multiplication and the lower-mask expression rely on signed wrap behavior not guaranteed by standard Fortran. C array-seeding code explicitly differs from reference initialization and is excluded. Source inspection does not establish period, bitwise agreement or statistical quality; no generator was run.

local.name: glmnet MATLAB builds
local.description: MATLAB interfaces and builds of Fortran lasso and elastic-net regression code.

classifications.notes: The README identifies rebuilt GLMnet Fortran/MEX components and Windows/MATLAB-specific compatibility reports. Prebuilt binaries and speed comparisons are upstream reports; this does not independently verify every model family or MATLAB release.

The external ELNET entry computes an elastic-net penalized Gaussian multiple-linear-regression path. PARM interpolates ridge and lasso penalties; the covariance-update path standardizes data and uses coordinate updates with soft thresholding and coefficient bounds, then rescales compressed coefficients/intercepts to the original predictor scale. This is penalized regression, not ordinary least squares or robust-loss estimation. X, Y, W and CL may be overwritten. FLMIN>=1 selects the user-supplied lambda sequence; LMU, IA and NIN describe the returned compressed paths and should be used rather than treating CA as a full coefficient matrix. Positive JERR denotes fatal error and negative JERR can retain earlier partial solutions. The source declares default REAL, so standalone callers must match that kind or a deliberately promoted whole build; MATLAB double arrays do not change the raw Fortran declarations. Review covers the dense covariance-update path and penalty iteration, not sparse/multivariate families or cross-validation selection.

procedures.summary: External dense Gaussian elastic-net path driver returning compressed coefficients.
procedures.usage:
external :: elnet
integer,parameter :: n=6,p=2,nlam=3
integer :: jd(1),ia(p),nin(nlam),lmu,nlp,jerr
real :: x(n,p),y(n),weights(n),vp(p),cl(2,p),lambda(nlam)
real :: intercept(nlam),coef(p,nlam),rsq(nlam),used_lambda(nlam)
x(:,1)=[0.,1.,2.,3.,4.,5.]; x(:,2)=[0.,1.,0.,1.,0.,1.]
y=[1.,3.,4.,6.,7.,9.]; weights=1.; vp=1.; jd=0
cl(1,:)=-100.; cl(2,:)=100.; lambda=[1.,0.1,0.01]
call elnet(1,0.5,n,p,x,y,weights,jd,vp,cl,p,p,nlam,1.,lambda,1e-5, &
 1,1,100000,lmu,intercept,coef,ia,nin,rsq,used_lambda,nlp,jerr)
if(jerr/=0) error stop "inspect regression path status"
! For each k<=LMU, COEF(1:NIN(k),k) belongs to predictors IA(1:NIN(k)).
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Default-REAL dense Fortran fragment; preserve copies of overwritten inputs and match any real-promotion flags across all objects/callers. No lambda selection, coefficients, fit accuracy or MATLAB wrapper execution was tested.

classifications.notes: The external LOGNET NC=1 path computes elastic-net penalized binomial logistic regression by iterated weighted/quadratic approximation and coordinate-descent updates. Y has two nonnegative count/weight columns even for NC=1, with column one defining the modeled event probability; rows are normalized internally and their totals become observation weights. G supplies offsets and is mutable working/output state. The routine dispatches the native LOGNET2N branch and rescales compressed coefficients after fitting. Positive row totals and both outcome classes are required; degenerate class probabilities, allocation, iteration and active-set limits have JERR conventions. The adopted GAMS regression tree has no dedicated penalized logistic/GLM leaf, so broad L8 is retained rather than labeling this nonlinear least squares or Gaussian regression. Review covers the dense binomial selection, normalization and penalized update paths, not multinomial/Cox/Poisson families, inferential coverage or predictive validation.

local.name: Nonnegative Matrix Factorization example
local.description: Fortran nonnegative matrix factorization using a multiplicative-gradient approach.

classifications.notes: The README describes reconstruction and rank-dependent representation size; combining it with k-means is an overarching goal. It does not establish a completed clustering pipeline or a guarantee of globally optimal/nonunique factor recovery.

factoring initializes W/H and alternates multiplicative updates involving W-transpose*A and A*H-transpose, with additive 1e-10 denominator offsets. K1b2a records its intended nonnegative bilinear least-squares matrix approximation: factor entries have linear nonnegativity constraints, unlike an SVD. Implementation findings limit use: w_update loops over H dimensions rather than W dimensions, causing incomplete/out-of-bounds updates for common reduced ranks; init_start_h declares width SIZE(A,1) but fills SIZE(A,2). The reported Error squares the sum of signed residuals, not the Frobenius residual norm. factoring runs a fixed iteration count and only prints reconstruction, returning a printing-helper integer rather than W/H or an optimizer status. No low-rank fit or convergence was verified.

procedures.summary: Public default-REAL function executing and printing an NMF experiment. Inputs A, rank and max_iter; return is an integer helper result, not factors or error status. The sketch uses square/full-rank dimensions solely to avoid the recorded rectangular/rank-loop mismatch.
procedures.usage:
use mu_method, only: factoring
real :: a(2,2)
integer :: printing_result
a=reshape([1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0],[2,2])
! Interface-only square/full-rank case; reduced-rank paths need the recorded repairs.
printing_result=factoring(a,2,5)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is a source-inspected experiment, not a checked dimensionality-reduction example. Fix w_update loop extents, init_start_h shape and the residual diagnostic before relying on general NMF use. Initialization calls nonstandard RAND and does not expose a local RNG state. Validate nonnegative finite input, rank and independent Frobenius residual yourself; no factor-quality assertion was run.

local.name: Spaloess
local.description: Spatial locally weighted regression adapted from R loess Fortran code.

classifications.notes: The README identifies modified distance calculations, Euclidean/great-circle choices and kd-tree controls. This supports spatial regression, not a standalone universal spatial-index library or verified prediction accuracy.

LOWESD initializes the packed LOESS workspace and LOWESF evaluates direct local polynomial fits through nearest-neighbor selection, distance weights, a local design matrix and QR/SVD-based least-squares work. XTDIST=1 selects Euclidean distances; XTDIST=0 selects the modified great-circle distance calculation with its assumed angular convention. The sketch restricts itself to Euclidean fits, finite data, positive span, valid degree 0..2 and initialized workspace. LOWESD version must be 106; IV/WV layout and per-coordinate degree controls must match the C workspace setup. LOWESF is an evaluation pass using supplied observation weights, not by itself the complete robust-reweighting workflow. Diagnostics call C/R EHG182/printing support rather than returning a general INFO dummy. Review covers setup/direct-fit dispatch and selected local weighting/design/solve paths, not the optional spatial distance model or validated smoothness/fit accuracy.

procedures.summary: External direct LOESS-fit entry requiring initialized IV/WV workspaces and C/R diagnostic support.

external :: lowesd,lowesf
! Allocate IV(LIV), WV(LV) following the author C LOESS_WORKSPACE formulas.
! X(N,D), Z(M,D), Y/WEIGHTS(N), FIT(M) are double precision.
! Choose enough noncoincident observations for a full-rank local polynomial.
call lowesd(106,iv,liv,lv,wv,d,n,span,degree,nvmax,.false.)
! Apply compatible per-coordinate/nonparametric controls as in the C setup.
ihat=0; xtdist=1
call lowesf(x,y,weights,iv,liv,lv,wv,m,z,l_dummy,ihat,fit,xtdist)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-allocation Euclidean direct-fit fragment; L_DUMMY must be addressable matching-real storage even with IHAT=0. local.name: Higher Order Markov Fortran
local.description: Fortran higher-order Markov transition fitting and prediction with C bindings.

classifications.notes: The README describes state-space extension and pure functions but its dependency URL is a placeholder. Fitting/prediction examples, zero-overhead claims and the shared-library build workflow were not tested here.

PREDICT_K_STEPS propagates an initial probability row vector through a finite-state transition matrix by repeated vector-matrix products. PREDICT_NEXT_STEP applies MATMUL(state_vector,transition_matrix), establishing the row-stochastic orientation. This is exact finite-step probability propagation up to floating-point arithmetic, not random path simulation or a continuous-time Markov solver. Broad stochastic-modeling class M is retained because the adopted taxonomy has no explicit finite-state discrete-time probability-propagation leaf; M1b is not inferred from the word Markov alone. The routines do not validate dimensions, nonnegativity, row sums, state-vector normalization or step counts. Negative K_STEPS simply leaves the original state under the loop semantics, so the sketch restricts K>=0. Review covers these pure first-order routines, not ergodicity, stationary distributions or the separate greedy higher-order trajectory routine.

procedures.summary: Public pure finite-step probability propagation using a row-stochastic transition matrix.
procedures.usage:
use iso_c_binding, only: c_double,c_int
use markov_core, only: predict_k_steps
real(c_double) :: transition(2,2),initial(2),future(2)
transition(1,:)=[0.8_c_double,0.2_c_double]
transition(2,:)=[0.3_c_double,0.7_c_double]
initial=[1._c_double,0._c_double]
future=predict_k_steps(initial,transition,3_c_int)
print *,future,sum(future)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use normalized nonnegative row probabilities and a conforming square matrix. The pure Fortran module API uses C interoperable kinds but is not itself a BIND(C) interface. No distribution, normalization drift or stochastic trajectory was tested.

classifications.notes: FIT_TRANSITION_MATRIX estimates a higher-order categorical transition table from an ordered state sequence. It encodes each length-ORDER history in base N_STATES, counts the following state and normalizes each observed-history row. An entirely unseen history receives a uniform row; this is a fallback, not Laplace smoothing of all observed counts. The result has N_STATES**ORDER rows and N_STATES columns, so storage and integer exponent/index overflow grow rapidly with order. Require state labels in 1..N_STATES, positive state count/order and enough sequence entries. There is no input-validation or statistical-status output. This is categorical time-domain model estimation, not linear autoregression, and broad L10a2 is kept rather than forcing an AR estimation leaf. The separate higher-order k-step routine chooses successive MAXLOC states and is not a full probability forecast; that routine is not used by this sketch.

procedures.summary: Public pure history-count estimator for a finite higher-order categorical transition table.
procedures.usage:
use iso_c_binding, only: c_double,c_int
use markov_higher_order, only: fit_transition_matrix,predict_higher_order_next
integer(c_int) :: observations(8)
real(c_double) :: transition(4,2),next_probability(2)
observations=[1_c_int,1_c_int,2_c_int,1_c_int,2_c_int,2_c_int,1_c_int,1_c_int]
transition=fit_transition_matrix(observations,2_c_int,2_c_int)
next_probability=predict_higher_order_next([1_c_int,2_c_int],2_c_int,transition)
print *,next_probability
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Small two-state order-two table; validate encoded states and exponential table size before calling. The final call extracts a one-step conditional probability row, not a multi-step distribution. No fitted table, unseen-history fallback or forecast was tested.

local.name: Contour 531
local.description: Modern Fortran wrappers producing contour polylines from sampled scalar grids.

classifications.notes: The README identifies ACM TOMS 531; regular-grid routine comments document uniform Cartesian spacing and repeated endpoints for closed contours. Closed-contour orientation is unspecified, and topology/degenerate-level behavior was not independently checked.

The README identifies ACM TOMS 531; regular-grid routine comments document uniform Cartesian spacing and repeated endpoints for closed contours. Closed-contour orientation is unspecified, and topology/degenerate-level behavior was not independently checked.

The regular-grid wrapper traces an isoline at a specified level through rectangular scalar samples using GCONTR, collects callback vertices into allocated polylines, then maps fractional grid indices to physical coordinates CORNER+(INDEX-1)*STEP. Closed contours repeat the starting point, with no guaranteed orientation. POLYLINE stores N_POINTS, CLOSED and POINTS(2,N_POINTS). This is contour extraction for plotting, not a complete rendering backend, an arbitrary unstructured mesh algorithm or certified topology at saddle/degenerate values. ZMAX excludes values above a threshold; NaNs need separate handling. Scratch arrays and contour counters are shared saved state, so simultaneous calls need serialization. Source dispatch, crossing tracing, collection and coordinate conversion were inspected; no contour image or topology test was executed.

procedures.summary: Module subroutine returning allocated polylines for one level on a regular grid. CORNER and STEP have two elements; all coordinates/scalars use default REAL.

local.name: PFAPACK Rust bindings
local.description: Rust bindings bundling Fortran PFAPACK routines for skew-symmetric matrices and Pfaffians.

classifications.notes: The short Rust-binding README is supplemented by the bundled Fortran example guide, which documents dense/banded Pfaffians and skew-symmetric decompositions. The build tag records the documented Make-based Fortran examples, not a verified Rust packaging workflow; this is a binding/distribution of PFAPACK rather than a separate algorithm.

DSKTRF computes a pivoted Parlett-Reid congruence factorization of a real skew-symmetric matrix, P*A*P^T=L*T*L^T or U*T*U^T. D2a1 is used only for this related factorization in the real nonsymmetric general-storage branch; it does not assert a solver for every nonsymmetric matrix. MODE=N fully tridiagonalizes, while MODE=P performs the partial even-order reduction used for Pfaffians. The driver chooses blocked DLASKTRF or unblocked DSKTF2 panels, propagates zero-pivot INFO and adjusts permutations. It overwrites the selected triangle with tridiagonal entries and multipliers. DSKPFA is also annotated as the public Pfaffian consumer of this reduction; it returns a Pfaffian, not a determinant, and reports zero for odd order. No new QR/SVD classification is inferred from this congruence reduction. BLAS/LAPACK-compatible support and the remaining PFAPACK kernels are required; this review inspects dispatch and Pfaffian accumulation, not all panel arithmetic.

procedures.summary: External double-precision skew-symmetric factorization with workspace query and pivot array.
procedures.usage:
external :: dsktrf
double precision :: a(4,4),query(1)
double precision,allocatable :: work(:)
integer :: piv(4),info,lwork
a=0d0; a(2,1)=-1d0; a(3,1)=-2d0; a(4,1)=-3d0
a(3,2)=-4d0; a(4,2)=-5d0; a(4,3)=-6d0
call dsktrf("L","N",4,a,4,piv,query,-1,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "workspace query failed"
lwork=max(1,ceiling(query(1))); allocate(work(lwork))
call dsktrf("L","N",4,a,4,piv,work,lwork,info)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Only the lower triangle is supplied; the full mathematical matrix is skew-symmetric. local.name: tfQMRgpu
local.description: GPU transpose-free quasi-minimal-residual sparse linear solves with Fortran interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README documents complex block-sparse tfQMR solves, multiple right-hand sides and Fortran 90/77 entry points. CUDA implements the computational backend. The public TFQMRGPU_BSRSV_COMPLETE wrapper solves complex non-Hermitian sparse A*X=B using block-sparse row patterns for A, B and the allowed solution X. It delegates to a private rectangular helper that creates a GPU handle/plan, uploads block data, calls the transpose-free QMR core, downloads X and frees resources. The core performs two TFQMR half-steps with sparse multiplications and per-RHS residual/breakdown tracking. Solution sparsity is prescribed by the caller, so a restricted X pattern is not equivalent to an unrestricted dense solve. Block sizes must have been compiled into the CUDA backend. Fortran patterns are one-based; block transposition flags are n/t, not an arbitrary conjugate-transpose operator. ITERATIONS/RESIDUAL are input limits and output reports. Helper CheckError uses STOP on many failures despite an IERR argument; core completion can include breakdown-stopped RHSs, so verify the reported and independently computed residual even after a successful status. Review covers the square-block convenience API and selected recurrence/stopping paths, not all precisions or block configurations.

classifications.notes: The README documents Fortran/C/C++ kernels exposed through Python tooling, including reductions, robust summaries and rolling analysis. The public SAFE-mode HPCS_MEDIAN/MAD/QUANTILE entries provide nonparametric location, dispersion and quantile summaries. They copy inputs, select order statistics by quickselect, average middle values for even-size medians, and interpolate quantiles with h=1+(n-1)*q. MAD is the raw median absolute deviation without a Gaussian consistency multiplier. SAFE mode propagates NaN with HPCS_SUCCESS rather than omitting it; callers must check both status and finiteness. Invalid n/q/mode returns do not promise an initialized numeric output, and NaN q is not rejected by ordinary range comparisons. Very large finite values can overflow middle-value averaging or interpolation differences. Explicit SAFE selection avoids the thread-local global mode; FAST/deterministic branches are not numerically validated here. Review covers public dispatch and SAFE calculations, not performance or rounding-error certification.

DLININT1 evaluates piecewise-linear interpolation on strictly monotone coordinates, with exact sentinel handling and optional removal of missing input values. The selected sketch uses ascending coordinates, ICYCX=0 and IOPT=0: no extrapolation is performed; out-of-range outputs and intervals touching missing data stay XMSG. Provide NXI>=2, NXO>=1 and separate work arrays, conservatively NXI2>=NXI+2; supported IOPT values are 0/1, with no rejection of other values. Independently validate coordinates and retained sample count: missing-value filtering can leave fewer than two nodes while the interpolation kernel accesses a pair. Single output coordinates are treated as ascending by the validator, so decreasing inputs with a single query can be rejected. DLINMSG separately fills interior missing runs on equally spaced sample indices in place. Its length threshold applies to interior and leading gaps, but the trailing MFLAG<0 continuation branch ignores MPTCRT. All-missing input remains missing. Missing values use exact sentinel equality, not NaN semantics. Cyclic extension and the internal short-gap optimization are outside the selected calling paths.
