classifications.notes: DLININT2 performs separable linear interpolation on a rectilinear two-dimensional grid: X interpolation of each input row followed by Y interpolation of the intermediate field. FI is dimensioned (NXI,NYI), FO (NXO,NYO). Require at least two nodes on each input axis, nonempty output axes, strictly monotone coordinates with matching input/output direction, finite exact missing sentinel, and supported IOPT=0/1. The reviewed calling path uses ascending complete data, ICYCX=0, IOPT=0 and separate NXI+2 work arrays. IER=1 reports dimensions, 2 X-coordinate validation and 3 Y validation. Filtering IOPT=1 can leave fewer than two valid nodes and must be guarded by the caller; it is not a scattered-data method, conservative remapper or missing-data extrapolator. The same direction flag is reused after both coordinate checks and passed into both interpolation stages: use axes with the same direction, as in the sketch; independently increasing X and decreasing Y is not safely supported by that implementation.

classifications.notes: COMPUTE_SEN_SLOPE returns the median of all pairwise slopes (Y(j)-Y(i))/(j-i), a robust simple trend-slope estimate for unit-spaced observations. It constructs reciprocal index lags and dispatches to the public precomputed-lag variant, which materializes N*(N-1)/2 slopes and uses selection rather than a full sort; even counts average the two middle values. Require clean finite REAL64 data, a separate slope workspace of that size, and sample counts whose integer products/indices fit the compiler integer kind. N<2 returns quiet NaN. This is a slope per sample interval, not a full regression result: no intercept, confidence interval, p-value, time-coordinate array or missing-value removal is returned. Removing gaps before calling changes the time spacing and therefore the problem. Memory and pair construction are quadratic; no large-series performance claim was executed.

The public ARMA_ACVF function forms theoretical autocovariances for a supplied causal ARMA model using a state transition/loading representation and fixed-point iteration of the stationary state covariance. It then propagates lag vectors to extract covariance at lags zero through MAX_LAG. These are model-implied covariances, not estimates from a sample. The sketch uses a stable AR(1), positive innovation variance and explicitly allocated empty MA coefficients. Invalid lag/variance returns an empty array; covariance iteration is capped and a failure returns HUGE-valued entries rather than a general status. A finite-value test alone does not reject that finite sentinel, and this routine does not independently prove model stability. Review covers state representation, iterative covariance and lag extraction, not the many unrelated translated time-series packages in the repository.

procedures.summary: Public theoretical ARMA autocovariance calculation returning an allocated zero-based lag array.

classifications.notes: ARMA_FORECAST uses a supplied ARMA model, theoretical covariance and the innovations recursion to recover sample innovations and extend the centered AR/MA recurrence. It adds the sample mean back and builds normal prediction intervals from accumulated squared infinite-MA weights times innovation variance. This is ARMA forecasting L10a2d3, not model selection, parameter fitting or a parameter-uncertainty interval. Even for a supplied model, centering uses the current sample mean rather than a stored model intercept. Require allocated AR and MA arrays, stable valid parameters, positive variance/horizon and a confidence level strictly inside (0,1). The returned INFO distinguishes input/innovation errors, but the covariance helper finite-HUGE sentinel warrants additional model/diagnostic validation. Review covers forecast recursion, innovations dispatch and interval construction, not empirical coverage or all transformed/nonlinear variants.

classifications.notes: The public BURG_FIT helper estimates univariate autoregressive coefficients by forward/backward prediction-error recursion. It demeans the series, computes reflection coefficients from paired errors, updates AR coefficients and innovation variance, then forms an approximate covariance matrix using an empirical Toeplitz matrix inverse. This supports AR parameter estimation, not automatic order selection or a global likelihood optimum. Input order must be positive and smaller than sample size; zero variance, degenerate error denominators, vanished innovation variance and failed covariance inversion have INFO returns. Reflections are clipped to [-1,1], and equality at a boundary can drive the variance failure path, so the header stable claim is not used as an unconditional guarantee. Review covers the native shared Burg implementation rather than only the ITSMR wrapper; covariance outputs are approximations, not verified inferential coverage.

local.name: Polynomial Arnoldi GMRES
local.description: Fortran GMRES and polynomial preconditioning experiments for a two-dimensional Poisson operator.

classifications.notes: The README is a placeholder, so the review uses documented interfaces in the pinned module and its FPM manifest. The operator is typed as Poisson2D rather than an arbitrary user matrix. This broad mapping does not validate stability control, zero-residual handling or general convergence.

polynomial_arnoldi::gmres builds a Krylov basis using twice-applied modified Gram-Schmidt, applies Givens rotations to a Hessenberg least-squares problem and updates X through a triangular solve, restarting when the subspace fills. D2 records this linear-system solver implementation. The public API is hardwired to external SpecialMatrices::Poisson2D, not a general dense/sparse matrix or arbitrary operator callback, so no unrestricted matrix-storage subclass is inferred without a dependency implementation review. The tolerance is internal ATOL+RTOL*NORM(B), with no caller tolerance/status dummy. A zero RHS is normalized before an early-exit check, and the total iteration cap is tested only at outer-cycle boundaries using <=; a full cycle can exceed it. Happy-breakdown/zero rotations and triangular pivots need independent validation. It prints a final true residual but returns X even if the budget is exhausted. Polynomial-preconditioned variants/root extraction and dependency kernels are outside this review. No solve or convergence experiment was run.

local.name: QuadProg modern Fortran
local.description: Active-set solution of strictly convex dense quadratic programs, with constrained least-squares helpers.

classifications.notes: The README describes a modernization of Turlach Quadprog using BLAS/LAPACK and currently real64 arithmetic. It targets strictly convex, small to moderate dense problems; indefinite/nonconvex QP support is not inferred. Its standard-compliance and performance claims were not tested here.

The standard qp_problem constructor copies and Cholesky-factorizes a positive-definite quadratic matrix, stores its inverse triangular factor, and records linear equality/inequality rows. solve_standard_qp packs constraints and calls the private qpgen2 active-set implementation. The reviewed driver starts at the unconstrained quadratic minimizer, selects violated constraints, computes primal/dual steps, adds constraints with Givens rotations and removes constraints when a dual step requires it. G2e1 records positive-definite-Hessian quadratic programming; no indefinite or merely semidefinite extension is inferred. The objective is 0.5*x-transpose*P*x - x-transpose*q, with A*x=b and C*x>=d; sign and row orientation matter. The constructor checks dimensions but does not propagate TRTRI INFO, and its Cholesky call has no returned err argument. The unconstrained wrapper branch sets X and success but never assigns result%obj; the sketch therefore uses a constrained case. The boolean success loses detailed driver failure information, so validate returned feasibility/stationarity independently. Compact storage, least-squares/LASSO variants and external numerical kernels are not audited. No QP or author tests were executed. The linked inequality test transposes C despite the constructor row-storage interface; that example orientation needs checking and is not copied into the sketch.

procedures.summary: Public generic constructor for the dense standard problem. P(n,n) must be symmetric positive definite, q(n) gives the SUBTRACTED linear term. Optional A/b and C/d must occur in pairs, with one constraint per ROW. All arrays use dp=selected_real_kind(15,307). The constructor stores a factorization rather than the original P; reconstruct the object when changing P and preserve originals for residual/KKT checks.
procedures.signature: problem = qp_problem(P, q, A=A, b=b, C=C, d=d)

procedures.summary: Public generic, scoped to the standard qp_problem overload. Input problem is INTENT(IN); private working copies are modified. Returns OptimizeResult with x, multipliers y (equalities followed by inequalities), obj and success for a constrained solve. Check success before using outputs. The unconstrained return path leaves obj unset.

use QuadProg, only: dp, qp_problem, OptimizeResult, solve

local.name: Bessel-Hankel
local.description: Fortran Bessel-function examples and numerical Hankel transforms using published filter/quadrature methods.

classifications.notes: The README documents Bessel values, derivatives and zeros, with inherited Moreau routines or intrinsic functions selected by preprocessing. Its Guptasarma/Singh filter is restricted to first-kind orders zero and one. Examples and formulas are not independent accuracy checks or evidence of an unrestricted-order transform implementation.

The README documents Bessel values, derivatives and zeros, with inherited Moreau routines or intrinsic functions selected by preprocessing. Its Guptasarma/Singh filter is restricted to first-kind orders zero and one. Examples and formulas are not independent accuracy checks or evidence of an unrestricted-order transform implementation.

HankelJ0Transform/HankelJ1Transform evaluate fixed logarithmic digital-filter sums of a kernel callback at lambda_i=10**(a+(i-1)*s)/r, then divide the weighted sum by r. Fast variants use shorter tables. J records numerical Hankel integral transforms; the original GAMS J subtree has no dedicated Hankel child, so neither Fourier nor Laplace classification is invented. The exact convention is integral_0^infinity K(lambda)*J_order(r*lambda) d(lambda), without an additional lambda measure factor. Callers using the common lambda*d(lambda) convention must incorporate lambda into K. R must be positive and finite, with a kernel defined over the sampled positive range; extreme R can overflow/underflow sampling. No error estimate, convergence status or adaptive quadrature is returned. Ogata/Bessel-zero paths are not included in this digital-filter review. No transform or published example was run.

procedures.summary: Public module function returning KIND(1d0), with scalar R and a legacy implicit-interface kernel callback EXTFunc(varName,lambda). The first argument is CHARACTER(*) and is passed the literal "lambda"; the second is REAL(KIND(1d0)). This is not a one-argument integrand ABI. KV is private; use an independently matching kind.

use Hankel_Transform, only: HankelJ0Transform
use example_Functions, only: exampleFunc1,myKind

reference=exampleFunc1("r",1._myKind)
! Independently compare value/reference; no error/status is returned.

Compile both modules in the snippet; R=1 avoids the singular R=0 interface. Do not insert an extra lambda weight unless your desired transform convention requires it. local.name: SAM Fortran library
local.description: Legacy Fortran finite-element matrix assembly, linear solves and eigenvalue support.

classifications.notes: The README marks the repository read-only and no longer maintained and documents BLAS/CMake dependencies. The sparse solver defaults to 64-bit integers. Algebraic support inside finite-element workflows is distinguished from a complete multiphysics application; ABI compatibility and numerical results were not checked.

SKYSOLVE solves a symmetric skyline/profile-stored system by unpivoted LDL-transpose factorization, forward reduction and back substitution. MSKY locates each diagonal in the packed upper profile, and A/B are overwritten by factors/intermediate values/solutions. The selected full-system usage sets NEQ1=NEQ and IFLAG=3; other flags split phases, and NEQ1<NEQ supports reduction outside this selected sketch. The routine replaces zero or sufficiently small pivots and records corrections in DCOR, with IERR=-3 indicating singular/poor conditioning correction; positive IERR=3 flags negative factor diagonals. This is not an unrestricted pivoted indefinite solver, and a corrected system is not silently equivalent to the original. Initialize all DCOR entries before factorization: the preliminary loop resets only its first column while later negative-flag suppression can inspect other columns. Use positive EPS/SCALE and valid skyline bounds, compatible BLAS/default-integer ABI, full SAM dependencies and a valid log unit or LPU<0 to suppress diagnostics. Preserve originals and check IERR/NND plus an independently recomputed residual. Negative IFLAG suppression and reduced-system semantics are not certified by this source review.

local.name: TOOLIB
local.description: Fortran numerical tool collection with a documented sparse-direct-solver interface.

classifications.notes: The reviewed MSOLV README describes wrappers for MUMPS, UMFPACK, SuperLU and MA48 with separate external-library requirements and restricted parallel configurations. Only this supported broad algebra scope is assigned now; the wider discovery-list inventory needs separate component reviews. The solvers are external backends rather than new TOOLIB implementations.

The public CHOLDC/CHOLSL pair factors and solves a real symmetric positive-definite dense system. CHOLDC reads the original upper triangle, stores strict lower factors in A and diagonal factors in P, leaving the upper input triangle in place. CHOLSL performs forward/back substitution using those factors. Require 1<=N<=NP, conforming REAL64 arrays and positive definiteness; there is no pivoting or symmetry test. Nonpositive computed pivots set INFO=1 and return incomplete factors; check before solving. CHOLSL treats INFO as input/output and returns immediately only when it equals 1, so pass the factorization status, not an uninitialized integer. Source comments credit Numerical Recipes; this mapping is source inspection, not a claim about complete third-party rights or numerical stability for arbitrary matrices.

classifications.notes: MOINDRES_CARRES_LINEAIRE constructs JF-transpose JF and JF-transpose HIJ, then uses the local Cholesky pair to solve the normal equations. JF has NB_PTS rows and NB_VAR columns; require NB_PTS>=NB_VAR>0 and full column rank for the unregularized solve. This is unconstrained real linear least squares, not rank-revealing QR/SVD or a robust rank-deficient solver. Forming normal equations squares the design-matrix condition number. INFO from Cholesky is local and not returned; the routine still copies SCD to BETA after failure. It also passes the same SCD buffer as both solve B and X; strict aliasing/conformance behavior was not validated. Independently validate rank, residual and output before relying on the fit.

classifications.notes: MOINDRES_CARRES fits a scalar response at supplied two-coordinate sample locations using user model F and parameter-derivative DF callbacks. It periodically rebuilds the Jacobian (every ten iterations), forms normal equations, inflates each diagonal by 1.5, solves with Cholesky and applies a fixed RELAX-scaled correction to the first NB_VAR_DER parameters. This is a particular damped, periodically updated Gauss-Newton-like implementation, not a complete adaptive Levenberg-Marquardt/trust-region API. Require 0<NB_VAR_DER<=NB_VAR and compatible derivatives/design rank; callbacks must match the linked signatures and their parameter array is declared INTENT(INOUT). The relative correction stop divides by ABS(BETA) without zero guards, and there is no maximum-iteration limit or complete failed-factorization exit. INFO reports the local Cholesky state, not a convergence certificate; the same-buffer solve finding from the linear fitter applies. The commented calling contract is not recommended for unattended execution before adding termination/failure guards.

classifications.notes: INTERP1D refines an evenly spaced one-dimensional grid by a factor of two. It copies coarse values to even indices and evaluates fixed midpoint Lagrange stencils of order 1,3,5 or 7 at odd indices. Endpoint ghost samples use linear derivative continuation. This is index-grid prolongation rather than an arbitrary-coordinate interpolation routine. The body explicitly accesses indices 0..UB_GROS and writes 0..2*UB_GROS despite lower-bound arguments; use zero lower bounds and sufficient source extent (at least ORDRE) and output storage. Unsupported ORDRE stops. High-order interpolation can overshoot and is not conservative or monotonicity-preserving merely because it reproduces polynomials. The private coefficient-generation helper is not a public interpolator.

classifications.notes: INTERP2D applies the public one-dimensional factor-two interpolation along each axis of an evenly spaced Cartesian grid, first into an intermediate table and then into the final grid. Its TBORNE arguments carry declared array bounds, but the underlying operation assumes coarse axes 0..N and fine axes 0..2*N. Use matching zero lower bounds, fine upper bounds exactly twice coarse bounds and a supported order 1/3/5/7 with sufficient source extent on both axes. This is separable gridded polynomial prolongation, not scattered-data fitting, geographic remapping or general independent target coordinates. No error status, input-shape validation or conservation guarantee is provided.

classifications.notes: The selected TAB_INIT_FFTW3/TAB_CALC_FFTW3/TAB_END_FFTW3 path allocates independent two-dimensional complex FFTW buffers/plans indexed by OpenMP thread number. Initialize outside the work region with NB_THREADS_FFT at least the maximum participating thread count; keep dimensions and that count fixed until cleanup. The module has shared allocation state and is not an independent per-object context. Both transform directions divide by SQRT(LONG*LARG), giving symmetric/unitary normalization. Important sign convention: this module defines FORWARD=+1 and BACKWARD=-1 and passes those directly to FFTW, whose include defines FFTW_FORWARD=-1 and FFTW_BACKWARD=+1. Thus the module FORWARD uses the positive-exponent direction, opposite FFTW standard naming. Use the linked module constants with awareness of that convention. Build with OpenMP enabled and compatible FFTW double-complex interfaces/libraries. No direction validation, allocation-status return or general null-plan check is exposed here; initialize once, calculate as needed, then clean up before reinitializing. Review covers this selected multi-buffer wrapper path and planner dispatch, not FFTW kernels or all alternate real/single-buffer paths.

classifications.notes: SORT_ARRAY2 selects the integer(I4) in-place ascending quicksort branch and carries an order vector through swaps; optional companion arrays are rearranged using that vector. This is active sorting, not just returning a rank vector. Supported dynamic array types are INTEGER(I4) and REAL(R8), with no default unsupported-type error; avoid other kinds/types. Require N>=1 because pivot selection occurs before the recursive base-case return. Real NaNs do not have an explicit ordering policy. The quicksort is not stable. If TAB0 is supplied, initialize it to a valid 1..N permutation (normally with INIT_ORDER); the same vector is used to index companion arrays, so arbitrary labels in TAB0 can cause out-of-range indexing or unintended permutation. No status or stable tie convention is provided.

classifications.notes: TCHEBY evaluates the first-kind Chebyshev polynomial T_N(X) using an explicit finite power/combinatorial expansion, with T_0=1 handled separately. TAB_TCHEBY allocates a table of degrees 0..DEG by repeated calls. Require N/DEG>=0 and finite arguments; the routine does not reject negative degree or diagnose overflow/cancellation. This implementation is not the stable three-term recurrence or a Clenshaw evaluator for a polynomial series, and high degree or poorly scaled X can cause severe cancellation/overflow. TAB_TCHEBY returns an allocatable REAL64 table (NX,DEG+1); allocation ownership follows its INTENT(OUT) contract. local.name: Fortran shape functions
local.description: Finite-element shape-function values and first/second derivatives on reference and mapped infinite elements.

classifications.notes: The README documents Lagrange, serendipity and mapped infinite families, evaluated at points from the external fortran_cubatures package. Shape-function support is not a complete PDE solver or an independently checked cubature library. Invalid inputs stop the program; author test/compiler claims were not reproduced.

The README documents Lagrange, serendipity and mapped infinite families, evaluated at points from the external fortran_cubatures package. Shape-function support is not a complete PDE solver or an independently checked cubature library. Invalid inputs stop the program; author test/compiler claims were not reproduced.

For the explicitly selected finite line element, SHAPEFUNC constructs nodal Lagrange polynomial basis functions and EVAL evaluates them at a requested reference coordinate. An interpolated value is the dot product of nodal data with returned basis values. This E1b mapping is restricted to the univariate polynomial case; it does not conflate reference-element shape functions with scattered-data mesh generation or global spline fitting. Node ordering can be permuted through NODES, so the sketch forms data from the returned COORDS instead of assuming a particular edge/interior order. SET requires a cubature object from the separate fortran_cubatures dependency; invalid setup can ERROR STOP. Review covers finite Lagrange line construction/evaluation, not every simplex/serendipity/infinite-element variant or an executed interpolation result.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound reference-element basis/value/derivative evaluator; all result arrays are required.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use cubatures, only: cubature,CUB_LIN
use shapefuncs, only: shapefunc
type(cubature) :: q
type(shapefunc) :: sf
real(real64),allocatable :: nodal(:),basis(:),derv(:,:),curv(:,:,:)
real(real64) :: value,first,second
q=cubature(CUB_LIN,4)
sf=shapefunc(q,2)
allocate(nodal(sf%nnodes),basis(sf%nnodes),derv(1,sf%nnodes),curv(1,1,sf%nnodes))
nodal=sf%coords(1,:)**2
call sf%eval([0.25_real64],basis,derv,curv)
value=dot_product(nodal,basis)
first=dot_product(nodal,derv(1,:))
second=dot_product(nodal,curv(1,1,:))
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Finite line/polynomial example using the separate cubatures dependency and REAL64. Derivatives are with respect to reference XI, not automatically physical coordinates. No interpolation, node-order or partition-of-unity check was run.

classifications.notes: SHAPEFUNC%EVAL also returns analytic first and second derivatives of each basis function in reference coordinates. LAGRANGE propagates value/first/second derivatives through product factors; EVAL_PRODUCTS assembles mixed derivatives and applies the constant factor-coordinate chain rule, symmetrizing curvature. This is numerical evaluation of analytic basis derivatives, not finite-difference differentiation of an arbitrary callback. Physical-space gradients/Hessians require the appropriate geometric mapping, including extra terms for nonaffine maps; returning reference curvature does not perform that transformation. Infinite directions have singularities at XI=1. The selected sketch uses a finite line and differentiates an interpolated nodal polynomial. type(shapefunc) :: sf

FA_KF_PREDICT applies x=F*x and P=F*P*F-transpose+Q. FA_KF_UPDATE computes innovations, gates individual measurements by squared innovation over diagonal innovation variance, extracts the retained full covariance submatrix, solves the SPD innovation system, and applies a Joseph-form covariance update. All C-boundary matrices are flat row-major, not ordinary Fortran column-major arrays. VALIDITY is output: +1 fused, 0 skipped above 9, -1 rejected above 16 (or degenerate diagonal); if no values are fused, state/covariance remain at prediction with INFO=0. Cholesky solve failure maps to INFO=4; invalid dimensions to 3. Covariance consistency/finite values are not comprehensively checked. Some helper calls alias input/output arrays despite differing INTENTs and need compiler/alias-contract review. The sketch uses a scalar model to avoid layout ambiguity. Review covers the linear KF path and matrix-solve helper, not every EKF/UKF/particle-filter variant.

interface
 subroutine fa_kf_predict(n,x,p,f,q,info) bind(C)

  integer(c_int) :: info

 subroutine fa_kf_update(n,m,x,p,z,h,r,validity,info) bind(C)
  import c_int,c_double
  integer(c_int),value :: n,m
  real(c_double) :: x(n),p(n*n),z(m),h(m*n),r(m*m)
  integer(c_int) :: validity(m),info
 end subroutine
end interface
real(c_double) :: x(1),p(1),f(1),q(1),z(1),h(1),r(1)
integer(c_int) :: validity(1),info
x=0d0; p=1d0; f=1d0; q=0.1d0; z=0.2d0; h=1d0; r=0.25d0

call fa_kf_update(1_c_int,1_c_int,x,p,z,h,r,validity,info)

DPCG uses diagonal-preconditioned conjugate gradients for a symmetric positive-definite sparse operator. BICGSTAB performs preconditioned nonsymmetric Krylov iteration using forward/back substitutions with an incomplete diagonal factor, while GAUSSSEIDEL updates entries sequentially from CSR row residuals. The BiCGStab routine reports ILU(0), but its structural searches assume matching transpose entries and valid pivots; an absent counterpart can leave a search beyond the row. Restrict the selected sketches to ordinary CSR systems with NOC=0: initial BiCGStab residual includes cut-coupling AL/AR but the two iteration matrix products omit it; Gauss-Seidel has those extra terms commented out entirely. BiCGStab divides by shadow-product and factor quantities without a complete breakdown-status policy. Gauss-Seidel stopping uses residual values collected during sequential updates rather than a freshly evaluated simultaneous residual of the final iterate. Matrices must satisfy conditions for the chosen iteration to converge; this is not an arbitrary sparse direct solver. The generic LINEAR_SOLVER file has repeated placeholder selectors, so these cards identify the actual external routines rather than endorse that dispatcher.

LININTERPOL searches for neighboring abscissae and evaluates an affine weighted pair, using a saved interval index for subsequent calls. The implemented interpolation is univariate piecewise linear. Despite header prose promising zero outside the table, those returns/assignments are commented out; search conditions may evaluate negative/out-of-range elements and the final formula extrapolates after clamping. The nold<1 check does not reject a one-point table. Even an in-range query on a two-point table can first read beyond the upper end because the saved-index clamp sets nold-1 then accesses ilastnum+1. Resetting ILASTVAL sets ILASTNUM=-1; a subsequent upward search can begin at -2 and read a negative index even for an in-range query. More table points do not repair this. The sketch records the interface only; the search requires repair and checked testing before use. This review does not establish flux conservation or review the spectral-resampling dispatcher.

procedures.summary: External subroutine using numeric RP=8 and IB=4 kinds from ModDataType. Table/query/output vectors use dummy lower bound zero; NOLD_VEC/NXYVALUE are explicit lengths. ILASTVAL is input/output (negative resets saved search state), ISKEEPON is output and VERBOSITY optional. An explicit interface is required.
procedures.signature:
CALL LINinterpol(XX_VALUE, YY_VALUE, NXYVALUE, XOLD_VEC, YOLD_VEC, &
     NOLD_VEC, ILASTVAL, ISKEEPON, VERBOSITY)
procedures.usage:
use ModDataType, only: rp,ib
! Supply the linked explicit interface including OPTIONAL VERBOSITY.
real(rp) :: x(0:2), y(0:2), query(0:0), value(0:0)
integer(ib) :: last,status
x=[0.0_rp,1.0_rp,2.0_rp]; y=2.0_rp*x
query=[0.5_rp]; last=-999_ib
call LINinterpol(query,value,1_ib,x,y,3_ib,last,status,0_ib)
! Inspect STATUS, but it does not certify bounds safety or accuracy.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is an interface sketch, not a recommended safe general interpolator. The source search/bounds findings need repair and checked testing. Saved ILASTNUM makes the core nonreentrant; resetting ILASTVAL is essential after changing tables. Numeric kind constants are compiler-dependent. Direct callers supply lengths hidden by F2PY.

The public INTERP_LINEAR generic implements adjacent-point piecewise-linear interpolation for scalar/vector queries; INTERP_SPLINE builds cubic piecewise-polynomial coefficients and evaluates them. Require equal nonempty X/Y lengths, finite strictly increasing distinct X and at least two points for the spline. Linear queries outside the interval clamp to endpoint values. Spline outside queries use reflection about the endpoint and a reflected value, rather than the same constant policy; farther outside reflected arguments may themselves leave the interval. The cubic helper solves a tridiagonal coefficient system with its own endpoint conditions, not a user-selectable natural/clamped boundary API. No status argument validates sorting, duplicate nodes or model error. The defining helper source credits an earlier Godunov interpolation implementation; component provenance remains scoped.

procedures.summary: Public generic for scalar or vector adjacent-point linear interpolation.

use interp1D, only: interp_linear

classifications.notes: The public INTERP_BILINEAR generic selects a double-precision rectangular tensor-grid path which brackets each query on two ordered coordinate axes, linearly combines four neighboring values and preserves a missing sentinel where interpolation is unavailable. Z is shaped (SIZE(X),SIZE(Y)); the reviewed overload returns (SIZE(XOUT),SIZE(YOUT)), with MASK on the output grid. Strictly increasing axes with at least two nodes and matching finite data are required. Queries equal to either extreme coordinate are marked outside by the <=/>= tests; only strictly interior points are interpolated. Any sentinel-valued corner prevents interpolation. FILL is accepted/stored but the filling block in this overload is commented out; it does not fill missing outputs. This is a source review of the gridded overload, not the separate paired-query or nearest-neighbor variants, scattered triangulation or conservative remapping.

procedures.summary: Public bilinear generic, selected double-precision Cartesian-product query overload.
procedures.usage:
use coord_constants, only: dp
use interp2D, only: interp_bilinear
real(dp) :: x(2),y(2),z(2,2),q(1),out(1,1)
x=[0._dp,1._dp]; y=x
z=reshape([0._dp,1._dp,1._dp,2._dp],[2,2]); q=0.5_dp
out=interp_bilinear(x,y,z,q,q)
! Queries on outer grid edges return the missing sentinel in this overload.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Strictly interior query only. FILL has no active filling implementation here. No interpolation value, mask or missing-data behavior was executed.

classifications.notes: The public LOESS_SMOOTH generic regularizes an irregular series onto a uniform grid, calls the native LOWESS local-linear smoother with two robustness iterations, then linearly maps the smoothed series back. It omits Y equal to the chosen missing sentinel, uses the minimum consecutive X spacing to allocate the uniform grid, and derives F from L, DX and grid size; require sorted distinct X, at least two points and a practical minimum spacing to avoid huge allocation. L is not simply a point-count window; the code uses (2*L+1) in both its availability gate and fraction formula. It prints L/F and returns the sentinel when its point-count gate fails. The double overload explicitly casts data/window to default real before computation; its output is not a full double-precision LOWESS calculation. The same repository offers FILTER_GAUSSIAN via normalized sampled Gaussian weights and reflected boundary patches. Explicitly supply positive DX: the float path starts with SIGMAP=SIGMAP and only assigns a value when DX is present, and the double wrapper evaluates REAL(DX) without a PRESENT guard. The double Gaussian overload also reduces the field to REAL(4). Kernel width must fit the convolution implementation; its four-pass fallback is not an unlimited large-kernel remedy. These are smoothing implementations, not uncertainty estimates, missing-NaN detection or a precision guarantee.

procedures.summary: Public LOWESS smoothing generic; selected double interface computes through default-real data.

yfit=loess_smooth(x,y,l)

procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-data-setup fragment. Validate minimum spacing, uniform-grid memory and missing sentinel before use. No smoothing result or robustness property was tested.

classifications.notes: The public CONVOLVE routine accumulates weighted two-dimensional patches after reflecting each side once. Its implementation multiplies weights in their stored orientation without reversing them: for general asymmetric weights this is a correlation-style operation; symmetric Gaussian weights implement the corresponding convolution. H2/J2-style scalar integral or Fourier transform APIs are not inferred from the name. Inputs, weights and outputs are REAL(4), output must match input shape and weights should have odd extents so patches conform. Each weight extent must be strictly less than the corresponding input extent+1 (checked with an assertion that can terminate). Without MASK it is a direct weighted patch sum. With MASK, excluded centers remain unchanged and weights of excluded neighbors are redistributed equally over included neighbors; this is not a general theorem of global field conservation. The kernel is not automatically normalized and no sentinel/NaN policy is provided.

procedures.summary: Reflected-boundary weighted patch correlation; symmetric weights give convolution.

field=1.0; weights=1.0/9.0
call convolve(field,weights,out)
! Symmetric normalized odd-sized weights; no mask in this fragment.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Odd kernel smaller than the supported reflection extent. No output, boundary treatment or conservation property was tested.

classifications.notes: HGRAD returns the magnitude of a centered finite-difference horizontal gradient, not a two-component gradient array. Its private helpers divide by 2*DX and copy neighboring interior derivatives to boundaries. Require positive finite DX and at least three points in each direction. A concrete boundary-index defect is present: D_DX assigns DU(NY,:) rather than DU(NX,:), so nonsquare grids can leave the last row wrong or address beyond the first extent. Restrict the sketch to square grids or repair this before general rectangular use. NORM=.TRUE. divides by MAXVAL(ABS(DU)) without a zero guard, so constant fields may divide by zero. Review records the local stencil and its limitations, not a general nonuniform/curvilinear gradient, convergence study or corrected implementation.

procedures.summary: Magnitude of a uniform-grid horizontal finite-difference gradient; square-grid restriction at this pin.
procedures.usage:

! U is a finite REAL(4) square grid, at least 3 by 3.
! The pinned D_DX boundary index needs repair before nonsquare-grid use.
magnitude=hgrad(u,dx=1.0,norm=.false.)
! Avoid normalization of constant fields without adding a zero guard.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-data-setup fragment explicitly restricted to square grids. No derivative, boundary or zero-gradient behavior was executed.

classifications.notes: The public CREATE_POLYGON and POINT_IN_POLYGON generics build a planar polygon from coordinate arrays and classify query points by parity of ray/edge intersections. The selected constructors assemble sequential edges closing the polygon; the query creates a default-real point and counts intersections over stored index pairs. Supply matching finite coordinate vectors, at least three sensible vertices and a valid simple polygon. The implementation perturbs a query Y equal to a vertex Y by a fixed EPS=1e-5, and slope/vertical-edge comparisons use floating-point thresholds. Consequently boundary/vertex inclusion, scale dependence and degenerate/self-intersecting polygons are not certified exact predicates. This is planar point containment, not spherical geometry, triangulation or polygon Boolean operations. Allocatable polygon components carry copied points/edge indices; the explicit FREE_POLYGON helper is private.

MCM returns the arithmetic mean of each column of a double-precision matrix by straightforward sequential summation and division by the number of rows. Calling with one column provides a univariate raw-data location summary; multiple columns are treated independently, not as a joint model. Require N>0, positive column count, matching storage and finite prefiltered data. There is no missing-value, overflow, compensated-summation or recoverable status policy. This records the implemented descriptive statistic, not an inferential estimate with uncertainty or a robustness guarantee.

procedures.summary: External arithmetic column-mean routine; one-column use gives a scalar mean.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(4,1),mean(1)
x(:,1)=[1.d0,2.d0,3.d0,4.d0]
call MCM(4,1,x,mean)
! No status or missing-data handling is returned.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Require nonempty finite columns; naive summation can lose accuracy for large offsets or cancellation.

classifications.notes: VARIAN computes sample variance as (SUM(X**2)-SUM(X)**2/N)/(N-1); VOLAT calls it and takes a square root except that variance below a fixed 1e-30 threshold is returned as zero. Both set INFO=-2 for fewer than two observations. The one-pass difference-of-squares formula is vulnerable to cancellation and can produce a negative computed variance for poorly scaled inputs; VOLAT then silently returns zero rather than reporting that loss of accuracy. Require finite data and inspect scale/conditioning independently. These routines are raw-data dispersion summaries, not confidence intervals, robust scale estimators or an accurate two-pass variance implementation.

procedures.summary: External sample variance with N-1 denominator and a cancellation-prone one-pass formula.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(4),variance
integer :: info
x=[1.d0,2.d0,3.d0,4.d0]
call VARIAN(4,x,variance,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect variance input length"
! Independently assess cancellation for large-offset data.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Finite raw-data fragment; INFO=0 is not an accuracy check.

procedures.summary: External sample standard deviation with a fixed small-variance zero convention.
procedures.usage:
! X(N) is a finite DOUBLE PRECISION vector with N>=2.
call VOLAT(n,x,stdev,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect standard-deviation status"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-data-setup fragment. Small or negative computed variances are mapped to zero, so validate scaling independently.

classifications.notes: SKEWN and KURTOS accept a raw sample plus a caller-supplied mean and variance, accumulate third/fourth central powers and apply explicit finite-sample formulas. SKEWN requires N>=3 and variance>=1e-15; KURTOS requires N>=4 and variance>1e-15. The mean/variance must describe the same sample and use a compatible convention; these are not independently estimated inside the routines. SKEWN initializes INFO=0, but KURTOS assigns INFO only on failure and leaves it unchanged on success: initialize it before calling. The header labels the kurtosis unbiased excess kurtosis, but the hand-coded expression is retained as implementation evidence rather than certifying equivalence to the usual bias-corrected estimator. Neither formula, overflow behavior nor sample distribution was numerically validated. These are descriptive shape calculations, not normality tests or confidence intervals.

procedures.summary: External third-moment shape calculation using supplied sample location/variance.
procedures.usage:
! After computing a compatible DOUBLE PRECISION mean and sample variance:
call SKEWN(n,x,meanx,variance,skewness,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect skewness length and variance"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-statistics-setup fragment. Require N>=3 and nondegenerate variance; no shape result was tested.

procedures.summary: External fourth-moment/excess-kurtosis expression; success does not reset INFO.
procedures.usage:
! With a compatible sample mean/variance and N>=4:
info=0
call KURTOS(n,x,meanx,variance,kurtosis,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect kurtosis length and variance"
! Validate the estimator formula before interpreting the result.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-statistics-setup fragment with explicit status initialization. No unbiasedness, formula agreement or result was tested.

classifications.notes: COVM computes column means, centers N by P observations through EMPCOV and forms the sample covariance; CORM normalizes it to a correlation matrix. Require N>=2, P>=1 and finite complete data. COVM needs DWORK(P*(N+1)); CORM actually needs P*(N+P+2), as its header states, despite a shorter conflicting workspace comment. CORM returns INFO=-5 when a variance is <=1e-30. The underlying COVR scales by 1./FLOAT(N-1), evaluated in default real before assignment, so this factor can have lower precision than the double arrays. COVCOR and CORCOV convert a supplied covariance/correlation matrix and standard deviations; COVCOR rejects diagonals <=1e-30, while CORCOV does not validate a correlation matrix or standard deviations. These are descriptive/representation operations, not hypothesis tests, missing-data estimation or certification of positive definiteness. Although some headers mention a mean vector, COVM has no separate named mean output; its first P workspace entries contain the means.

procedures.summary: External complete-data sample covariance using explicit workspace.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(4,2),work(10),cov(2,2)
integer :: info
x(:,1)=[1.d0,2.d0,3.d0,4.d0]; x(:,2)=[4.d0,1.d0,3.d0,2.d0]
call COVM(4,2,x,work,cov,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect covariance status"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. N by P column-major complete data and P*(N+1) workspace. No covariance or conditioning result was tested.

procedures.summary: External empirical correlation matrix; constant columns are rejected.
procedures.usage:

call CORM(n,p,x,work,correlation,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect correlation status, especially constant columns"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-array-setup fragment with the full workspace size; no correlation result was tested.

procedures.summary: Convert correlation and standard deviations into covariance entries.

classifications.notes: TENSORK and TENSORKK calculate selected slices of third- and fourth-order empirical central co-moments from multivariate raw data. They compute column means, multiply centered coordinates with a fixed K (and L), average by N and fill a symmetric P by P output slice. These are unstandardized central moments, not dimensionless skewness/excess kurtosis, cumulants or unbiased corrected estimators. Require N>0, P>=1, valid fixed indices in 1..P, X(N,P), DWORK(P) and H(P,P). Invalid K/L returns INFO=-1000; N/P and input finiteness are not generally validated. The parent raw-data multivariate class is retained because its covariance/correlation child does not describe higher moments. Review covers these directly callable slice routines, not all higher-tensor wrappers or their differing workspace comments.

procedures.summary: External third-order central co-moment slice with fixed variable K.
procedures.usage:
! Initialize finite DOUBLE PRECISION X(N,P), WORK(P), HK(P,P).
call TENSORK(n,p,k,x,work,hk,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect fixed co-moment index"
! HK(I,J) averages centered X_I*X_J*X_K.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-data-setup fragment. Positive dimensions, matching storage and valid K are required; no co-moment was executed.

procedures.summary: External fourth-order central co-moment slice with fixed variables K and L.
procedures.usage:
! With matching DOUBLE PRECISION arrays and 1<=K,L<=P:
call TENSORKK(n,p,k,l,x,work,hk,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect fixed co-moment indices"
! HK(I,J) averages centered X_I*X_J*X_K*X_L.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-data-setup fragment. This is not excess kurtosis or a fourth cumulant; no value was executed.

classifications.notes: GETNORMALPDF evaluates the standard normal probability density as the stored approximation to 1/SQRT(2*PI) times EXP(-X*X/2). It is a density at a real argument, not a cumulative distribution, inverse quantile, sampling routine or nonstandard-mean/variance normal PDF. Match the DOUBLE PRECISION external function declaration in the caller. There is no status, scaled/log-density alternative or tail-accuracy guarantee; extreme X can underflow or overflow the intermediate square even when the true density is tiny.

procedures.summary: External double-precision standard-normal density function.
procedures.usage:
double precision,external :: getNormalPdf
double precision :: density
density=getNormalPdf(0.d0)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Scalar density fragment; no density normalization, tail or numerical value was tested.

classifications.notes: GENNOR implements location/scale transformation AV+SD*SNORM() of an Ahrens-Dieter/Forsythe-style normal generator. The inspected SNORM uses stored tables and acceptance/rejection paths supplied by RANF. This is an intended normal-sampling implementation, but the ordinary default-real call chain is defective: SNORM declares RANF as DOUBLE PRECISION while the provided RANF function returns default REAL. A compatible return ABI must be repaired or established explicitly before use. RANF also depends on preprocessing: INTELFOR invokes INIT_RANDOM_SEED on every draw before RANDOM_NUMBER; the other path uses the compiler-specific RAND intrinsic. Seed policy, endpoint behavior and parallel independent streams are not established here. Require positive finite SD and a validated uniform source strictly suitable for the rejection algorithm. The contract sketch is deliberately commented until these issues are resolved; no sample distribution, reproducibility or randomness quality was tested.

procedures.summary: External normal variate generator; the bundled uniform-return mismatch requires repair.
procedures.usage:
! Post-repair contract only: make SNORM/RANF return kinds and ABI agree,
! select a valid uniform source and initialize its seed policy once as intended.
! double precision,external :: gennor
! double precision :: value
! value=gennor(0.d0,1.d0)
! Do not rely on the unmodified mixed-return-kind chain.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Commented post-repair fragment. No generator execution, seed behavior, rejection path or statistical quality check was performed.

The scalar FZERO overload dispatches to NEWTON_INTERPOL, which uses two nearby initial function values and secant interpolation to solve a scalar equation without a supplied derivative. It is not a bracketing Brent solver despite other optimization routines in the toolbox. The selected cosine-minus-x example is a nonpolynomial equation and supports F1b. X is overwritten; the optional CHECK_RETURN is false on a residual-based return and true on stagnation or exhausted iterations. Shared module tolerance/iteration settings affect calls. The iteration has no interval or domain safeguard and can encounter a vanishing secant denominator; callers must supply a valid initial neighborhood and independently check the final residual. Review covers the scalar generic/implementation, not the distinct vector Broyden overload or global root isolation.

procedures.summary: Public scalar secant-style root solver selected through the FZERO generic.
procedures.usage:
program scalar_root_sketch
use toolbox, only: fzero
implicit none
real(kind=kind(1d0)) :: x
logical :: failed
x=0.5d0
call fzero(x,residual,failed)
if(failed) error stop "root iteration stagnated or reached its limit"
print *,x,residual(x)
contains
function residual(x) result(value)
 real(kind=kind(1d0)),intent(in) :: x
 real(kind=kind(1d0)) :: value
 value=cos(x)-x
end function
end program
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build the pinned toolbox and match its REAL*8 interface. The scalar overload does not bracket a root or prove uniqueness; inspect the residual even after CHECK_RETURN is false. No root, stagnation or domain-error case was run.

classifications.notes: The scalar POLY_INTERPOL generic evaluates the global Lagrange interpolating polynomial through supplied univariate nodes. The implementation builds each product basis directly and sums YI times the bases; it is not piecewise interpolation, a spline or a barycentric implementation. Equal node/value counts are asserted, but duplicate nodes are not rejected before division. Distinct well-scaled nodes and modest degree are appropriate for the calling sketch; polynomial interpolation does not imply stable extrapolation or freedom from Runge oscillation. The node/value dummy arrays have lower bound zero, which is reflected in the usage fragment. Review covers scalar evaluation and generic visibility, not the separate vector-query implementation or fitted-error guarantees.

procedures.summary: Public scalar global Lagrange polynomial interpolation through arbitrary distinct nodes.
procedures.usage:
use toolbox, only: poly_interpol
real(kind=kind(1d0)) :: nodes(0:2),values(0:2),value
nodes=[-1d0,0d0,1d0]; values=nodes**2
value=poly_interpol(0.5d0,nodes,values)
print *,value
! Distinct nodes are required; the routine does not guard duplicate abscissas.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This fragment uses three nodes for a quadratic and matches the toolbox REAL*8 arrays. It illustrates interpolation rather than a checked accuracy result. No value, high-degree stability or extrapolation case was tested.

classifications.notes: LEGENDRE generates Gauss-Legendre abscissas and weights on a finite interval, selecting order from the output-array size. It uses symmetric initial root guesses, recurrence evaluation of Legendre polynomials/derivatives, Newton corrections and symmetric mapping of roots/weights to the target interval. The concrete mapping is quadrature service routine H2c: this API does not itself accept or integrate a user function, and the sketch performs the fixed-order weighted sum separately. Array-size mismatch or exhausted root iterations invokes the toolbox error handler; no numerical status is returned. The source caps root iteration at ten steps. A positive order and increasing finite endpoints are assumed by the sketch. The source explicitly identifies Numerical Recipes adaptation, which is retained as a licensing/provenance qualification rather than silently treating every component as original GPL code.

procedures.summary: Public fixed-order Gauss-Legendre node/weight generator on a caller-supplied interval.
procedures.usage:
use toolbox, only: legendre
real(kind=kind(1d0)) :: nodes(4),weights(4),integral
call legendre(0d0,1d0,nodes,weights)
integral=sum(weights*nodes**2)
print *,integral
! This weighted sum is caller-side quadrature; LEGENDRE returns nodes/weights.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Four-point fixed-order example, not automatic adaptive integration or an error estimate. Build the matching toolbox and consider retained component notices. Compare independently with 1/3; no nodes, weights or integral were tested.

local.name: ANN Fortran interface
local.description: Fortran/C interface to the C++ ANN exact and approximate nearest-neighbor library.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly expands ANN as Approximate Nearest Neighbors, not artificial neural networks. The underlying algorithms/data structures are C++, with Fortran access provided here. Approximation guarantees, high-dimensional performance and current build compatibility were not checked.

The Fortran ANN module forwards point-cloud construction and single-query k-nearest-neighbor search to the C++ ANN kd-tree. The bridge copies a Fortran point matrix with ROWS points and COLS coordinates using input offset I+J*ROWS; QUERY has DIM coordinates, compatible with the built tree. The backend uses EPS to relax search and returns zero-based point indices with squared Euclidean distances; EPS=0 selects exact search under the native algorithm. Require 1<=K<=ROWS and nonnegative EPS. Important reviewed defects prevent treating this as a ready-to-use ownership API: NNIDX/DISTS pointers are written into but never allocated by the bridge, so callers must supply live K-entry buffers; C++ temporary arrays are freed with scalar DELETE rather than matching array deallocation; the public Fortran destroy routine only nulls its handle, with its C destroy call commented out; construction point storage ownership is not released by that public path. The C destroy declaration also passes a pointer reference while the C++ definition takes a pointer value. Native search state uses file-scope globals, so independent concurrent search is not assumed. This is a mapping of the implemented kd-tree bridge with defects recorded, not a successful build, leak-free lifecycle, numerical verification or batch-query interface.

local.name: FortLearner
local.description: Fortran K-means kernels with thin Python bindings and OpenBLAS support.

classifications.notes: The current Japanese README identifies K-means with k-means++ initialization, labels stable distribution not yet released and describes Linux-focused test packaging. Older discovery claims about many additional learning algorithms are not carried forward. Cluster quality, persistence and non-Linux source builds were not tested.

The public KMEANS object fits dense nonhierarchical Euclidean clusters through repeated nearest-centroid assignments and centroid updates, with random/kmeans++ initialization, optional explicit initial centers, restarts and empty-cluster relocation. X has observation rows and feature columns; PREDICT returns one-based labels in an (N,1) allocatable INT64 matrix. SCORE returns a nonnegative-style sum of squared distances, not sklearn negative inertia. The selected sketch uses N_INIT=1 and default unchunked storage: the demo passes real-valued N_INIT/CHUNK_SIZE although the inspected constructor requires INT64, and the multi-restart chunked path passes the unallocated whole-distance matrix. The iteration helper also marks persistent input state INTENT(OUT) while reading it, and convergence checks can touch initially unset previous centroids. Those state contracts require repair/validation before relying on fits. OpenBLAS thread control and RNG state are global side effects. Review is source-based, not a validated clustering implementation.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound dense K-means training method; optional initial centers have shape (clusters,features).
procedures.usage:
use mod_kinds, only: i64,r64
use mod_kmeans, only: kmeans,new_kmeans
type(kmeans) :: model
real(r64) :: x(4,2)
integer(i64),allocatable :: labels(:,:)
x(:,1)=[0._r64,0.1_r64,4._r64,4.1_r64]
x(:,2)=[0._r64,0.2_r64,4._r64,4.2_r64]
model=new_kmeans(n_clusters=2_i64,n_init=1_i64,random_state=1_i64,num_threads=1_i64)
! Resolve the documented iteration-state INTENT/initialization issues first.
call model%fit(x)
labels=model%predict(x)

The public SELF_ORGANIZING_MAP%TRAIN binding fits a fixed-grid Kohonen prototype map through online best-match selection and neighborhood-weighted prototype updates. The reviewed normal_som path uses a decreasing learning rate/radius and Gaussian or bubble neighborhoods, then assigns patterns to final best-matching nodes. This is non-nested prototype clustering, not hierarchical clustering or a supervised predictor. Training needs a created map, compatible initialized KOHONEN_PATTERN objects and validated layer parameters; create randomizes prototype values using the configured generator. The implementation visits patterns in supplied order, has radius/learning-rate floors and writes progress/distortion information. The OpenMP best-match loop updates a shared argmin without a visible reduction/protection; use a serial build or one OpenMP thread for this scoped sketch. Empty/invalid dimensions, unsuitable scaling and all nonfinite distances are not certified. Review covers the public binding and normal_som best-match/update paths, not all ViSOM or two-level variants.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound online training of a created fixed-grid self-organizing map.

use self_organizing_map_utilities, only: self_organizing_map
use kohonen_layer_parameters_utilities, only: kohonen_layer_parameters
use kohonen_pattern_utilities, only: kohonen_pattern
type(self_organizing_map) :: map

! Set SOM_TYPE="normal_som" and a supported distance/neighborhood.
! NUMBER_PATTERNS and the variable dimensions must match PATTERNS.
! Use a serial build or one OpenMP thread for this fragment.
call map%create(parameters)
call map%train(patterns)
! Query/print the trained prototypes and assignments before cleanup.
call map%destroy()

The README explicitly excludes batch training, dropout, convolution and distributed parallelism and says alternative optimizers are not wired into network training. Proposed L-BFGS/classification/recurrent features are not counted. BLAS/LAPACK dependencies and supplied QR-versus-network comparisons were not tested.

The public NEURALNET%BACKPROP method differentiates the scalar network loss with respect to packed weights and optional biases by reverse propagation through activation derivatives and BLAS products. This is analytic chain-rule/backpropagation differentiation, not finite differences or a general source-transforming AD tool. WEIGHTS/BIAS are inout buffers: their entry values become model parameters and their returned contents become gradients. DATA uses predictor rows plus one target row and observation columns. The LOSS callback supplies derivative with respect to prediction, despite its name; the supplied MSE returns 2*(prediction-actual), with averaging performed inside BACKPROP. Activation callbacks distinguish forward value from derivative with FW. The method mutates network intermediate state and reports selected dimension failures via IERR. EVALUATE declares IERR INTENT(OUT) but does not set it on success; BACKPROP immediately tests that undefined value and likewise lacks an explicit final success assignment. Repair the success-status contract before relying on returned gradients. Review covers the scalar-output gradient path and interface, not arbitrary tensor AD, every activation at nondifferentiable points or verified gradient accuracy.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound scalar-network loss-gradient method with packed mutable parameter/gradient buffers.
procedures.usage:
use NEURALNET_MOD, only: neuralnet,MSE
! Build NET with matching input dimension and one output node.
! DATA(D+1,N) holds predictors then target; copy parameter values first.
! W and BIAS have exactly the network packed weight/bias lengths.
! First repair EVALUATE/BACKPROP success-status assignments.
call net%BACKPROP(w,bias,data,MSE,ierr)
if(ierr/=0) error stop "network gradient failed"
! W/BIAS now contain averaged loss gradients, not original parameters.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-construction fragment with compatible REAL_PRECISION R8 and BLAS doubles. Handle networks without biases carefully: the training path passes an unallocated bias buffer in that branch, whose safety needs investigation; this sketch assumes allocated biased layers. Compare against independent finite differences before use. No derivative, allocation or activation test was run. The success-path IERR defect must be resolved before the displayed status check is meaningful.

classifications.notes: The public OPT_MOD::ADAM module subroutine updates an unconstrained vector using a supplied gradient callback, exponential first/second moments and bias-corrected adaptive steps. The selected class describes smooth multivariate minimization with user-provided first derivatives; the method neither evaluates an objective nor supplies bounds/Hessians. IBUDGET limits gradient calls; an exactly zero gradient causes early return, but no norm-based convergence/error status is returned. Caller must choose valid decay/step/epsilon values and a suitable gradient. The SGD sibling uses geometric step decay; ADAGRAD is not promoted here because its inspected initial zero accumulator is tested for zero before the first accumulation, causing immediate return. Review covers the ADAM recurrence and callable contract, not optimizer convergence or network-training correctness.

procedures.summary: Public module gradient-only unconstrained optimizer with optional budget and moment controls.

use REAL_PRECISION, only: R8
use OPT_MOD, only: ADAM
real(R8) :: x(2)
x=[2.0_R8,-1.0_R8]
! Supply GRAD(D,X,G), for example G=2*X for the smooth sum-of-squares objective.
call ADAM(2,gradient,x,ibudget=1000,alpha=0.01_R8)
! Independently evaluate the objective and gradient norm at returned X.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Callback body omitted; import the module for optional arguments and match R8 kinds. NN_TL computes a Jacobian-vector product for the configured dense network while also returning the nonlinear output; NN_AD computes the transpose-Jacobian action on a supplied output seed. They apply analytic activation derivatives and ordinary/transposed BLAS GEMM through the layer sequence, recomputing nonlinear trajectories for the reverse path. SVDFIT forms a weighted linear least-squares design from the built-in FUNCS1 ENTRY, divides each row and response by SIG(i), factors it through local SVDCMP, zeros singular values below 1e-14 of the maximum, and applies SVBKSB. It is linear in fitted coefficients of a permutationally invariant polynomial basis in exp(-distance), not nonlinear parameter fitting or a generic callback-based fitter. PREPOT must previously initialize saved basis tables, MPI state and COMMON model/training distances as in the application driver; FUNCS1 is an ENTRY in that initialized routine. Require positive finite weights/scales, 1<=MA<=NDATA<=MAXDATA, MA<=MAXTERM and MA<=MAXDATA for local SVD buffers, MP>=NDATA and NP>=MA, matching includes/COMMON layout and sufficient memory for U(MP,NP), V(NP,NP) and large static model arrays. The safest selected dimensions are MP=NDATA, NP=MA, matching the author call and avoiding the oversized NP dummy contract in SVBKSB. Only coefficients A are returned: CHISQ, U/V/W are local despite stale comments suggesting outputs. There is no exposed convergence/rank/error status; SVDCMP has a finite iteration loop but its nonconvergence PAUSE diagnostic is commented out. Recompute weighted residuals and assess rank independently; this is not a certified robust or converged fit.

The public SequentialNeuralNetwork tangent-linear and adjoint bindings propagate perturbations/cotangents through sequential layers. Unlike an input-only Jacobian API, DP includes packed parameter perturbations and the adjoint returns both parameter and input cotangents. Dense layers pack biases first, followed by the reshaped weight matrix. ADAPGAUSS generates an M-point Gauss-Legendre rule and adaptively bisects a finite interval, comparing a parent rule value with the sum of child values. The callback is a SUBROUTINE FUN(X,PAR1,PAR2,VAL), despite some comments calling it a function. Use matching REAL*8 parameter arrays/callback arguments; do not infer type-safe arbitrary integer user-data passing from historical comments. M must be positive and <=100 because local node/weight arrays have 100 entries. EPS>0 is compared independently against each accepted leaf difference: it is not divided among leaves and therefore is not a guaranteed global absolute-error bound. Depth is limited to 200 and the work loop to 100000 steps; IER=8/16 indicates those respective limits and RINT can be partial. MAXREC/NUMINT describe the traversal, not proof of error control. The rule differences can miss unresolved singularities/oscillations; no special weighted-integrand or rigorous error certificate is implied.

if(ier/=0) error stop "quadrature stopped at a subdivision limit"

classifications.notes: LEGEWHTS constructs nodes and optional weights for a fixed-order Gauss-Legendre rule on [-1,1]. It starts from cosine root approximations, uses up to ten Newton corrections and exploits symmetry; weights come from a sum-of-squared-Legendre orthogonality relation. IFWHTS=1 computes weights, 0 returns nodes alone. Choose the quadrature order yourself; no tolerance-driven integrand adaptation or error estimate is returned. Positive N and caller-owned TS/WHTS storage of at least N elements are required. The old dummy declarations TS(1)/WHTS(1) are indexed beyond their declared extent, a legacy source convention requiring attention under bounds/conformance checking. Newton termination is not reported by a separate status, so do not infer successful roots/weights for every order. The calling sketch shows how this rule would be applied to a smooth scalar integrand, not a checked polynomial-exactness test.

classifications.notes: LEGEPOL uses the Legendre three-term recurrence to return P_N(X), then computes its first derivative through N*(X*P_N-P_(N-1))/(X**2-1). Degree 0 and 1 have explicit value/derivative branches. Require N>=0; negative degree is not rejected. For N>=2, X=+/-1 gives a zero denominator and near-endpoint evaluation can lose derivative accuracy. Use interior finite arguments or separately supply mathematically appropriate endpoint limits; this pin does not implement such a special branch. This is evaluation of one Legendre polynomial and derivative, not evaluation of a whole fitted series, associated Legendre functions or a spherical-harmonic transform.

               iter, fcnt, istop)

classifications.notes: bmdfsaneacc::dfsaneacc solves a square system: the residual callback maps x(n) to res(n), with no Jacobian callback. It combines residual-direction nonmonotone steps with QR-based sequential-secant acceleration built from iterate/residual history. Success requires dot_product(res,res)<=epsf**2, so epsf bounds the residual Euclidean norm; iteration exhaustion is a distinct return. F2 is already a GAMS leaf: there is no official derivative-free or acceleration child to add. Internal least-squares acceleration is not evidence for a general rectangular least-squares solver, and this does not enumerate all roots or certify uniqueness. The Fortran example supplies a three-variable exponential system; the reviewed Fortran path does not require running R or CUTEst. Memory/rank limits, singular cases and the author example were not tested.

procedures.summary: Public generic array-reduction function. The inspected REAL(dp) binding accepts an assumed-shape vector and returns a scalar of the same kind; extrapol_rdp and its nested helpers are private implementation details. Supply equally spaced samples with 2**m+1 entries for the reviewed extrapolation path, and multiply the normalized result by the physical interval length.
procedures.usage:
use Extrapolation_Integration_Kinds, only: dp
use Extrapolation_Integration, only: extrapolation
! array is REAL(dp) with 2**m+1 equally spaced samples on [a,b].
result = (b - a) * extrapolation(array)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Initialize the samples and interval endpoints with compatible kinds. This function takes sampled values, not an integrand callback or error tolerance. The inspected non-dyadic fallback has the endpoint-weight discrepancy documented in the source review; the sketch deliberately uses the dyadic path. No accuracy or execution check was performed here. Other real/complex bindings are not newly certified by this interface review.

classifications.notes: The reviewed real(dp) extrapol_rdp path accepts equally spaced samples rather than an integrand callback, error tolerance or adaptive sampling request. It reorders 2^m+1 samples with endpoints first, constructs nested trapezoidal approximations and applies Richardson extrapolation. H2a1b2 is the nonautomatic finite-interval grid-quadrature leaf. The reduction is normalized to [0,1]; multiply by (b-a) for samples on [a,b], as the author sinc example does. A material fallback discrepancy was found by source inspection: non-dyadic sample counts are sent directly to trap_rdp, which half-weights array(1) and array(2), not the first and last samples in natural order. For [0,1/3,2/3,1] the displayed formula predicts 11/18 instead of the trapezoidal result 1/2; this is an arithmetic consequence of the source, not a compiled result. Singleton/two-point cases have separate branches; empty input and all accuracy claims remain unverified. No checked driver is supplied.

INFO is an input step budget (with sign-dependent mode) and an output status/sweep count, not solely a LAPACK-style output error code.
procedures.signature: CALL DKSVD0(JOB, N, G, LDG, U, LDU, V, LDV, SV, W, O, R, INFO)
procedures.usage:
! Follow the author DKSVD0X driver for JOB, INFO and workspace setup.
! Initialize G, leading dimensions, U/V as required, and the schedule O.
call DKSVD0(JOB, N, G, LDG, U, LDU, V, LDV, SV, W, O, R, INFO)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Use the exact declarations and preprocessed sources at this pin, including the shared included bodies. The driver allocates W(MAX(6,3*M)), generates the schedule with JSWEEP, and prepares O and R for its padded matrix size M; these requirements depend on the chosen strategy. Do not pass uninitialized INFO. The libpvn kernel boundary remains a dependency, and the source mapping covers the reviewed real square cyclic/quasi-cyclic path, not every compiler option, precision or rectangular variant. Not compiled or run here.

procedures.summary: Author SVD test program. Its included shared body parses strategy, matrix dimension and an input basename, initializes arrays/schedule and invokes DKSVD0. This catalog has not supplied its matrix input files or run the driver.

classifications.notes: The real64 DKSVD0 interface and its included gksvd0 body implement a two-sided Kogbetliantz SVD of a square N-by-N matrix. The body generates index pairs, extracts 2-by-2 pivots, applies left/right rotations, optionally accumulates U and V, and extracts singular values from the transformed diagonal. D6 is already a GAMS leaf, with no separate cyclic or precision subclass. This review follows the cyclic/quasi-cyclic real64 path, not every blocked, dynamic, complex or higher-precision variant. Some strategies require even N. DKSVD2 is a Fortran wrapper around the external libpvn PVN_DLJSV2 kernel; it is not an independent local implementation of that 2-by-2 algorithm. INFO carries an input step budget/accuracy mode and an output sweep count or limit, rather than a universal zero-success convention. Scaling, rounding assumptions, reconstruction, orthogonality and parallel performance were not tested; no rectangular-matrix claim is inferred from the repository title.

classifications.notes: The real dual-number path propagates first derivatives in a dx(ndv) vector through overloaded multiplication, division, exponential and sine operations. The inspected product, quotient and chain-rule formulas operate on values and derivative vectors, without finite-difference steps. auto_fill seeds identity derivatives separately for concentration and spatial-gradient variables, then extracts flux/reaction/accumulation Jacobian entries. This supports H1, already a GAMS leaf including automatic differentiation. It is forward first-order differentiation, not a Hessian or reverse-mode implementation. In this fork ndv=2*N depends on user_input, and the scalar real kind follows the build configuration; it is not a standalone precision-generic package without adaptation. The reviewed path does not establish correctness of every overload, complex extensions or nondifferentiable branches. The README credits inherited DNAD by Wenbin Yu/Maxwell Blair and the upstream fork; those components are not newly attributed to this repository. No derivative check or program was executed.

procedures.summary: Public BAND_mod assembly stage. It reads model coefficients from variables and writes the current block-band matrices for spatial node j. It must follow auto_fill(j); it is not an independent matrix-assembly API with explicit array arguments.

Public BAND_mod block-elimination/back-substitution stage for the model state at spatial node j. It reads and overwrites shared variables arrays and depends on sequential calls from j=1 through NJ after model assembly; it is not a general solver that accepts a matrix as an argument.
procedures.usage:
use BAND_mod, only: auto_fill, ABDGXY, BAND
! Model modules, mesh, initial conditions and work arrays are initialized.
do j = 1, NJ
   call auto_fill(j)
   call ABDGXY(j)
   call BAND(j)
end do
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Adapt the absolute include paths in both the model and BAND_MOD.f95 and compile modules in dependency order. N/NJ and variables arrays come from the selected model; the final spatial call performs back substitution. Singularity handling prints diagnostics and is not a robust solve-status API. The block system is not a scalar tridiagonal interface. No build, residual or PDE accuracy check was made.

procedures.summary: Public module routine used internally by BAND. It applies elimination to shared B and D arrays from variables, with N rows and M right-hand sides; DETERM is a default-real output diagnostic. The arrays are not dummy arguments, so this entry is exposed only for users adapting the model engine, not as a standalone inverse routine.

classifications.notes: ABDGXY assembles neighboring real blocks and BAND performs forward block elimination followed by back substitution, including special boundary couplings through X and Y. Each block solve delegates to MATINV, which applies Gaussian/Gauss-Jordan row operations to B and the multiple right-hand sides in D. The supported GAMS scope is real nonsymmetric banded linear systems (D2a2). Block tridiagonal structure is not generally scalar tridiagonal, and boundary terms can reach an additional neighboring block, so the D2a2a leaf would overstate the structure. This is an inherited Newman BAND-style specialized solver using module-global arrays, not a general LAPACK-compatible band-storage interface. NJ must accommodate the referenced neighboring nodes, and the routine assumes compatible block/boundary assembly. Singular-block diagnostics print and continue in BAND; conditioning, pivot robustness, residuals and larger systems were not checked. No complex or symmetric-positive-definite specialization is inferred.

procedures.summary: Author one-dimensional diffusion program. It initializes model state, loops over spatial nodes through auto_fill/ABDGXY/BAND, then updates cprev and time. Absolute include paths in the example and BAND_MOD.f95 require adaptation. This is a standalone model, not a generic PDE-solver subroutine.

classifications.notes: This mapping is restricted to the simple rectangular diffusion example, not the repository collection of physical applications. The author program sets one dependent variable, one spatial grid and a positive constant diffusivity; FLUX=-diff*dc/dx, RXN=0 and ACCUM=c/delT describe the one-dimensional parabolic diffusion initial-boundary problem. auto_fill forms finite-volume flux/accumulation derivatives; unsteady loops over spatial nodes through auto_fill/ABDGXY/BAND and updates the solution in time, with prescribed end concentrations. I2a1a is the GAMS leaf for parabolic PDEs in one spatial dimension. The example uses absolute author-machine include paths, and BAND_MOD uses another absolute path, so it is a source example requiring path adaptation rather than a portable checked driver. The included core wiring is inspected, but boundary compatibility, time accuracy, stability and mesh convergence were not checked. No general nonlinear iteration-convergence guarantee or multidimensional PDE mapping is added.
